target.title: fix(cron): emit scheduled events after durable wake changes
target.body:
Closes #103205.

## What Problem This Solves

External scheduler plugins can observe cron jobs being added, updated, removed, started, and finished, but they are not notified when OpenClaw changes an existing job's durable `nextRunAtMs` internally.

That leaves external wake schedulers stale after quiet trigger evaluation, recurring completion, retry backoff, startup deferral, or maintenance repair unless they poll the full cron list.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the already-documented `scheduled` action to the public `cron_changed` hook contract and emits it from the cron persistence boundary after an existing job's next wake actually commits.

The service keeps a process-local projection of durable next-run values, compares it only after successful saves, and publishes one reconciliation signal for each changed existing job. Explicit CRUD targets retain their existing `added`, `updated`, or `removed` event without a duplicate `scheduled` event; schedule repairs to sibling jobs still emit `scheduled`.

The implementation introduces no new config, environment variable, Gateway protocol method, or storage format.

## User Impact

Plugins can react promptly when OpenClaw durably reschedules or cancels an existing cron wake. A `scheduled` event includes the public job snapshot and `nextRunAtMs`; an absent value means the job is durably unscheduled.

`scheduled` is a best-effort post-commit reconciliation signal, not an ordered event log. Multiple committed transitions can occur close together, and hook handlers run asynchronously. Consumers should debounce or coalesce notifications, reconcile the full list through `ctx.getCron?.()?.list({ includeDisabled: true })`, and perform a full reconciliation on `gateway_start`.

Existing `finished` and automatic `removed` events keep their current lifecycle semantics; this change guarantees post-commit behavior specifically for `scheduled`.

## Evidence

- Store-level coverage for changed, cancelled, unchanged, failed-save/retry, force-reload, quarantine, topology, and explicit-update suppression behavior.
- Cron behavior coverage for quiet trigger evaluation, recurring completion/error backoff, retained one-shot cancellation, delete-after-run, and sibling schedule repair.
- Gateway hook propagation coverage verifies the public job snapshot and top-level `nextRunAtMs` match the committed job.
- Plugin hook typing and generated Plugin SDK API baseline include `scheduled`.
- Exact rebased-head focused proof: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx5ssjbv6rt3esxkmy459d1s`; [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29087038631). All 137 cron, Gateway, and plugin tests passed.

- Broad dependent proof: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx5rv905atrvrbvve5vmdvg8`; [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29086170953). Every touched cron, Gateway, hook, and plugin lane passed; the run stopped on one unrelated model-fallback probe logging assertion. Its exact 20-test file passed immediately in isolation on Testbox `tbx_01kx5skw54e0fk7pf7m4n79xa3`; [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29086879328).

target.title: fix(auto-reply): prevent block-reply coalescer from dropping tail text on abort/stop
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram DM block-streaming (`streaming.mode="block"`) silently drops the tail of long assistant replies. The last ~300–600 chars of a reply never arrive — the visible message ends mid-sentence with no error logged. (Issue #102578)

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause in `createBlockReplyCoalescer` (`src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.ts`):

1. **`flush({force:true})` at turn finalization was skipped by `shouldAbort()`** — when a prior block delivery had timed out during streaming, `aborted = true` was set in the pipeline (`block-reply-pipeline.ts`). The final force-flush then saw `shouldAbort() === true`, reset the buffer, and silently dropped the buffered tail text.

2. **`stop()` at pipeline boundary didn't reach `onBlockReply` after abort** — on error/recovery paths only `stop()` was called without a prior `flush()`. Any remaining buffered text below `minChars` was lost downstream when `sendPayload` returned early due to the `aborted` flag.

3. **No warning when text was discarded** — the silent data loss had no log trace.

### Fix architecture

Two-part fix that separates concerns cleanly:

**Coalescer layer** (`block-reply-coalescer.ts`):
- `flush({force:true})` now bypasses `shouldAbort()` — the caller explicitly requested data delivery.
- `stop()` only clears the idle timer; it no longer flushes. The pipeline owns drain before stop.
- `logVerbose` warning when abort discards buffered text, with context on force vs non-force flush.

**Pipeline layer** (`block-reply-pipeline.ts`):
- `sendPayload()` gained a third `bypassAbort` parameter. Coalescer-sourced payloads (via `onFlush`) pass `bypassAbort = true` so force-flushed tail text reaches `onBlockReply` even after the pipeline is marked `aborted`.
- The coalescer already gates abort independently via `shouldAbort()`; overlapping it at the pipeline level was the bug.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Telegram DM users with `streaming.mode="block"` lose the final ~300–600 chars of long replies silently, with no error or retry.
- **After**: The complete reply is delivered. All buffered text is flushed on finalization. If text is discarded via non-force flush during abort, a verbose log entry explains what was dropped.

## Evidence

### Unit test results

**New tests** (`src/auto-reply/reply/block-reply-coalescer.test.ts` — 9 tests, all passing):
- `force=true` bypasses `shouldAbort` — buffered text is flushed
- `stop()` does NOT flush; only clears idle timer
- `hasBuffered()` returns true after `stop()` when buffer has text
- `flush({force:false})` preserves default idle behavior
- `flush({force:true})` sends buffer even when under minChars
- Full pipeline simulation: tail text preserved across finalization
- Abort without force discards buffer
- Accumulated text >= maxChars triggers immediate flush

**Pipeline integration tests (all passing)**:
- `block-reply-pipeline.test.ts` — 26 pass
- Combined: 35 tests passing across coalescer + pipeline suites

### How the test proves the real scenario

The `full pipeline simulation` test replicates the exact gateway flow:
1. Stream large blocks accumulating without exceeding `maxChars`
2. Add the critical tail text that would previously be lost
3. Call `flush({force:true})` then `stop()` simulating finalization
4. Assert all accumulated text including the tail is delivered

### Logging

When abort discards buffered text, a `logVerbose` entry records the exact char count and whether the flush was forced or cancelled — enabling operators to detect silent data loss in production.

## How The Fix Was Tested

All tests pass with the latest `origin/main`.
No import cycles (`pnpm check:import-cycles`: 0 cycles).
Changed files: `block-reply-coalescer.ts`, `block-reply-pipeline.ts`, `block-reply-coalescer.test.ts` (net -2 LOC).

## Related

- Fixes #102578

target.title: fix(browser): respect --timeout-ms for browser evaluate command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Issue #103137 reports that `openclaw browser evaluate --fn "() => 1 + 1" --timeout-ms 60000` aborts after ~15 seconds, ignoring `--timeout-ms`. Long-running JavaScript evaluations on a live browser session cannot complete.

## Root Cause

The timeout is enforced by the gateway WS runtime (`server/ws-connection.ts:333-349`). It reads `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` from the client options, then passes it through `resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs()` from `packages/gateway-client/src/timeouts.ts`. When that value is `undefined`, the default is `DEFAULT_PREAUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`.

The bug was in `src/gateway/call.ts:callGatewayWithScopes()`: `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` was set to only `context.config.gateway?.handshakeTimeoutMs`. When that config key was unset (the common case for users who don't configure gateway handshake timeout), the value was `undefined`, and the runtime fell back to the 15s default — regardless of `--timeout-ms`.

## Fix

```diff
-    preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs: context.config.gateway?.handshakeTimeoutMs,
+    preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs:
+      context.config.gateway?.handshakeTimeoutMs !== undefined
+        ? context.config.gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs
+        : timeoutMs ?? undefined,
```

When `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs` is not configured, `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` now falls back to the request `timeoutMs`, which originates from the user's `--timeout-ms` flag.

## Evidence

### Gateway WS runtime timeout resolution log

The following output traces the actual production code path — from `call.ts` through `createGatewayClient({ preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs })` to `server/ws-connection.ts`:

```
=== Gateway WS runtime: preauth handshake timeout resolution ===
Production code path:
  src/gateway/call.ts - callGatewayWithScopes ->
  createGatewayClient({ preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs }) ->
  server/ws-connection.ts - resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs() ->
  setTimeout(timer, handshakeTimeoutMs)

DEFAULT_PREAUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000ms (hardcoded)

[BEFORE FIX] user runs with --timeout-ms 60000
  gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs = undefined (common case)
  preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs = undefined
  > resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs(undefined)
  > returns 15000ms
  > setTimeout(timer, 15000)  ← ABORTS at ~15s, --timeout-ms ignored!

[AFTER FIX]  user runs with --timeout-ms 60000
  gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs = undefined
  preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs = timeoutMs = 60000
  > resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs(60000)
  > returns 60000ms
  > setTimeout(timer, 60000)  ← --timeout-ms respected!

[EDGE] user configured handshakeTimeoutMs=30000
  gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs = 30000 (explicit)
  preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs = 30000 (handshake always wins)
  > resolvePreauthHandshakeTimeoutMs(30000)
  > returns 30000ms
  > setTimeout(timer, 30000)  ← handshake timeout preserved
```

### Actual gateway production log format when timeout fires (ws-connection.ts:344)
```
[warn] handshake timeout conn=abc peer=wss://127.0.0.1:18789 remote=127.0.0.1:54321 phase=pre-auth
```

### Regression test execution

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/call.test.ts -t "preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs|handshake timeout"
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  44 passed | 440 skipped

 ✓ passes configured gateway handshake timeout to the client watchdog
 ✓ falls back preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs to command timeoutMs when handshakeTimeoutMs is unset
 ✓ uses handshakeTimeoutMs even when timeoutMs is shorter
 ✓ falls back preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs to default timeout when neither is set
```

### Full test file — no regressions
```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/call.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  484 passed
```

## Files Changed

- `src/gateway/call.ts:1232-1235` — `preauthHandshakeTimeoutMs` falls back to `timeoutMs` when `gateway.handshakeTimeoutMs` is unset
- `src/gateway/call.test.ts` — 3 new regression tests covering all fallback paths

Fixes: #103137

target.title: feat(android): manage skills from settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android app had a read-only Skills settings surface while the Control UI already supports a fuller skills-management workflow. Android users could inspect gateway skill status, but they could not search installed skills, turn skills on or off, or install skills from ClawHub from the app.

This PR brings the requested Android skills-management path closer to the existing Control UI behavior while keeping Gateway policy as the source of truth.

## Summary

- Extend Android Skills settings from read-only status into a management surface with installed-skill search, Web-aligned status filters, and per-skill enable/disable via `skills.update`.
- Add ClawHub registry search and install from Android via `skills.search` / `skills.install`.
- Add an Android pre-install ClawHub audit review dialog before downloading a skill. The dialog resolves and displays:
  - skill name / slug
  - resolved install version
  - author / publisher
  - ClawHub audited safety result
  - security audit URL when provided
- Extend `skills.securityVerdicts` with a bounded explicit `items[]` request shape so clients can request pre-install review verdicts for known ClawHub slug/version pairs.
- Keep the security boundary server-side: Android cannot pass an arbitrary registry URL for verdict lookup; explicit verdict lookups resolve through the configured default ClawHub registry.
- Preserve Gateway trust enforcement: Android may acknowledge non-blocked review-required installs only from the review dialog; blocked/malicious releases remain blocked by Gateway policy.
- Parse `blockedByAgentFilter` for accurate Android skills status and keep the Android README/i18n inventory current.

## Web UI Reference Checked

Reviewed the existing Control UI skills implementation in:

- `ui/src/pages/skills/view.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/skills/skills-page.ts`
- `ui/src/lib/skills/index.ts`

Android now mirrors the relevant requested behaviors from the Web UI: installed-skill filtering/status grouping, global enable/disable, ClawHub search/install, and risk-aware install confirmation.

## Gateway/API Notes

- `skills.securityVerdicts` still supports the existing passive installed-skill verdict collection.
- New explicit mode accepts at most 25 `{ slug, version, ownerHandle? }` items.
- Explicit mode skips installed-skill scanning and fetches only the requested default-ClawHub verdict batch.
- Explicit mode projects the same sanitized fields as installed-skill mode; raw `security` payloads are not exposed.

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## Summary

Session-backed managed worktrees are now leased for the lifetime of every agent run. Idle GC waits for an admitted run to finish before it can snapshot or force-remove that checkout, including when the run uses a subdirectory inside the worktree.

## Root cause

GC's owner-activity read and `git worktree remove --force` were independent operations. The previous patch repeated the read closer to removal, but a session could still be admitted after that read and while the destructive command started.

## Fix

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease. `agent-command` acquires the lease before a session run touches its configured cwd and releases it in its outer cleanup. All managed removal paths acquire the same lease through snapshotting and git removal; idle GC retains the owner-active guard after it has obtained that lease.

Lease lookup accepts a managed worktree root or one of its subdirectories, matching session worktrees whose configured workspace is nested below the repository root.

## Why this is the right boundary

The worktree service owns the destructive operation and is the only place that can serialize it consistently with its consumers. Agent command is the session-run admission point that has the resolved cwd and can retain the lease through the actual runtime. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics, while an agent that loses the race before admission fails before using a deleted cwd rather than running against it.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: 24 passed.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts`, and `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core-test.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- Structured local review: no accepted or actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session must not have its managed checkout removed while its agent run is using that checkout or a nested workspace within it.
Real environment tested: pristine main `6eb9a5ada23b20353da9ef8e9fe69881567ca74f` and this patch `8a5ea1bac785439394ba6959fca805fa4231aee7`, driving the production ManagedWorktreeService against real on-disk git worktrees and filesystem state.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: create a session-owned worktree, start a lease from a nested directory, begin idle removal, confirm the directory remains present while the lease is held, release the lease, then observe the same queued removal complete.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 6eb9a5a)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: false
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: false
# AFTER (this patch 8a5ea1b)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: true
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: true
```
Observed result after fix: a live session retains its nested working directory until its lease ends, after which queued cleanup can complete normally.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the production worktree lifecycle and real git filesystem operations were exercised in-process.

## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needed a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. Existing setup and status paths could also leave stale native/container transport fields ambiguous, miss account-specific API-mode behavior, or report a Signal daemon as generically working when the configured account was missing or receive was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal plugin now owns a setup wizard path for two supported transports: local `signal-cli` and an existing Signal server managed by the operator. Users can run Signal setup, choose local `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, and have setup save config only after the selected transport is reachable for the intended account. target.title: fix(feishu): route outbound media by case-insensitive MIME type
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveFeishuOutboundMediaKind` (`extensions/feishu/src/media.ts`) compared the remote `Content-Type` with exact case-sensitive equality in its audio and video branches. MIME types are case-insensitive (RFC 2045), and `contentType` arrives from a remote URL's `Content-Type` header (`loadWebMedia`), which relays may emit mixed-case (e.g. `Audio/OGG`, `Video/MP4`). Such an outbound attachment was misrouted: a voice/audio clip became a generic `file` instead of `audio`, a video became `file` instead of `media`, and a mixed-case image header (`Image/PNG`) fell through `mediaKindFromMime` (also case-sensitive) to `file`. Feishu then renders the attachment as a flat file download instead of inline audio/video/image.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** `contentType` was compared raw (case-sensitive) in the audio/video branches, and `mediaKindFromMime(contentType)` is itself case-sensitive.
- **Fix:** lowercase `contentType` once at the top of `resolveFeishuOutboundMediaKind` via the already-imported `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty`, so the image (`mediaKindFromMime`), audio, and video branches all match consistently. The sibling `isFeishuNativeVoiceAudio` in the same file already lowercases the same way — this aligns the two functions.

## User Impact

Outbound Feishu attachments served with a mixed-case `Content-Type` are now routed to the correct message type (audio/video/image) instead of degrading to a flat file. Lowercase content types are unchanged.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Same RFC 2045 case-insensitivity class as the qqbot inbound fix a49567cdfd.

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node --import tsx` runtime verification calling the **patched router** `resolveFeishuOutboundMediaKind` (the function modified by this PR, imported from `extensions/feishu/src/media.ts`) on the exact PR head:

```
[PASS] mixed-case Audio/OGG: msgType=audio fileType=opus
[PASS] mixed-case Video/MP4: msgType=media fileType=mp4
[PASS] mixed-case Image/PNG: msgType=image fileType=-
[PASS] lowercase audio/ogg (regression): msgType=audio fileType=opus
[PASS] non-media pdf (regression): msgType=file fileType=stream
```

This calls the real `resolveFeishuOutboundMediaKind` (the function whose `contentType` comparison this PR lowercases), proving mixed-case MIME now routes to audio/media/image instead of degrading to file.

target.title: fix(signal): clean up signal-cli download temp dir on every exit path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`installSignalCliFromRelease` (`extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.ts`) creates a temp dir with `fs.mkdtemp` to stage the downloaded signal-cli archive, but never removes it. Every return path leaks the directory:

- the success return (line 361)
- the unsupported-archive-type early return
- the extraction-failure catch
- the binary-not-found error

signal-cli Linux-native archives are ~50-130 MB, and this is the only install path on Linux x64 (macOS uses Homebrew, Windows routes elsewhere). Every install — including the normal success path — leaves the full archive plus its temp dir behind. Repeated installs, retries, or CI runs accumulate multi-hundred-MB temp dirs under the preferred tmp dir indefinitely.

The sibling `downloadToFile` in the same file only removes the archive *file* on its own failure (line 174); it does not touch the parent temp dir, and on the success path neither the file nor the dir is removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** the body after `mkdtemp` had no `try`/`finally`; cleanup was simply missing on every exit.
- **Fix:** wrap the body in `try { ... } finally { fs.rm(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true }) }`, mirroring the established repo pattern for temp-dir staging (`src/plugins/marketplace.ts:downloadUrlToTempFile`, `src/skills/lifecycle/install-download.ts`, and the `withTempFile`/`withArchiveWorkspace` helpers in this file's own test suite all use `try`/`finally { rm }`).
- The extracted binary lives under `CONFIG_DIR/tools/signal-cli/<version>` and is untouched; only scratch download space is cleaned.

## User Impact

signal-cli installs no longer leak large download archives into the temp directory. Disk usage stays bounded across repeated installs/retries/CI. No change to the installed binary location or the install result.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node --import tsx` runtime verification exercising the **real `installSignalCliFromRelease` function** (the function patched by this PR) via its colocated test, plus a direct reproduction of the try/finally cleanup on a real filesystem:

```
[PASS] fixed flow: finally cleaned temp dir (no throw to caller)
[BEFORE] buggy flow temp dir exists: true (/tmp/openclaw-signal-buggy-XXXX)
[PASS] old pattern leaks temp dir (reproduces the bug)
```

The colocated test `install-signal-cli.test.ts` ("removes the download temp dir even when extraction fails") spies on `fs.mkdtemp`, calls the real `installSignalCliFromRelease` (only the network fetch is mocked; the install function and filesystem are real), drives it through a failing extraction, and asserts the created temp dir is gone (`fs.stat` rejects). It passed on the exact PR head:

```

  removes the download temp dir even when extraction fails (1 test, passed)
```

- **Canonical PR boundary:** #102627 is related only by Unicode root-cause class; it does not change diagnostics-otel content capture, JSON serialization, or OTLP export.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility and data-format/protocol behavior for captured OTLP attributes; no configuration, security boundary, message delivery, session state, or availability behavior changes.
- **Risk explanation:** The emitted JSON attribute is externally consumed by collectors. Splitting a surrogate pair can produce malformed `\\ud83d` JSON content even though the original capture text was valid.
- **Why acceptable:** The existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper retains the same UTF-16 budget except at the invalid split boundary, where dropping the high surrogate preserves valid JSON. Normal ASCII output, truncation suffix, redaction order, and exporter transport remain unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Oversized captured GenAI input messages can end on a lone UTF-16 high surrogate, causing the diagnostics-otel JSON attribute exported to OTLP to contain `\\ud83d` instead of valid Unicode text.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Trusted model-call input → private `modelContent` ingestion and GenAI message normalization → runtime OpenTelemetry span attribute → OTLP HTTP/protobuf export request effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** The private model-content input crosses diagnostic event ingestion, JSON serialization, the OpenTelemetry NodeSDK, and the OTLP HTTP/protobuf transport boundary before a collector receives it.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reviewed the existing repository Unicode helper and reused the already-imported `truncateUtf16Safe`; no provider parser, provider constraint, config schema, or default behavior changes.
- **Real environment tested:** Actual `createDiagnosticsOtelService()`, trusted internal diagnostics dispatcher, OpenTelemetry NodeSDK, HTTP/protobuf `OTLPTraceExporter`, and an isolated `127.0.0.1` collector with a temporary state directory.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran the local evidence driver below after rebasing onto current main; it emitted the trusted `model.call.completed` event, waited for the real exporter, and inspected the collector payload.

```text
tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.json "$EVIDENCE_DIR/otel-utf16-proof.ts"
```

- **Evidence after fix:** The same actual service-to-exporter path changed from a malformed surrogate escape before the patch to none after the patch.

```json
{
  "before": {
    "otlpRequests": 1,
    "malformedSurrogateEscape": true
  },
  "after": {
    "otlpRequests": 1,
    "malformedSurrogateEscape": false
  }
}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The loopback collector received one `/v1/traces` request and its binary protobuf payload no longer contained the JSON `\\ud83d` escape; the exact truncated content remains valid JSON.
- **What was not tested:** Out of scope: remote observability-SaaS ingestion and viewer rendering. This proof verifies the repository-owned service, exporter, and local OTLP protocol path without contacting a third-party service.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users and downstream collectors receive valid Unicode JSON for captured model content rather than replacement characters or malformed surrogate escapes at a deterministic truncation boundary.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** Emit the canonical trusted `model.call.completed` event with `x × 8177 + 🚀 + y × 140000`, parse `gen_ai.input.messages`, and assert the text is `x × 8177 + ...(truncated)` with no `\\ud83d` escape or lone high surrogate.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test enters through the same trusted content-capture path as production and reaches the source-of-truth truncation helper without adding a synthetic malformed object or test-only hook.

```text
pnpm test extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       108 passed (108)

pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json \
  extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts \
  extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
Exit code: 0
```

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `truncateJsonTextForOtelAttribute()` used `String.prototype.slice(0, prefixBudget)`, which counts UTF-16 code units. When the prefix boundary falls between an emoji's high and low surrogates, it creates a malformed lone surrogate that `JSON.stringify()` encodes as `\\ud83d`.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch changes the source truncation invariant before JSON serialization and before the span attribute is exported. It reuses the shared boundary-safe helper at the sole unsafe slice, rather than adding a downstream sanitizer, exporter fallback, or collector-specific workaround.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the repository-owned diagnostic capture and OTLP export path, based on a before/after local live proof, focused regression coverage, and type-aware lint of both changed files.
- **Patch quality notes:** Two-file focused diff; no casts, lint suppressions, fallback/default branch, schema change, lockfile churn, or unrelated formatting.
- **What did NOT change:** Redaction, the `...(truncated)` suffix, all JSON array/object/string budgets, capture-content configuration semantics, exporter endpoint/protocol selection, sampling, metrics, logs, and remote collector behavior are intentionally not changed.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** This is the source-of-truth runtime serialization path for exported span attributes, not a post-processed mirror. It does not change model input, model-consumed context, prompt history, or any user configuration contract.
- **Compatibility / contract scope:** Existing truncation limits and attribute shape remain compatible; only a malformed Unicode boundary now removes the incomplete code unit, preserving valid JSON rather than changing normal or ASCII content.
- **Out of scope:** No public API, config schema, protocol version, remote collector implementation, or observability viewer is changed.

target.title: fix(gateway-client): clamp readiness timeout before client start
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers using an explicit gateway client readiness timeout could pass an oversized finite value that reached the readiness waiter without the safe timer clamp used by the default timeout path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The explicit timeout path now reuses the existing finite timeout delay resolver with the same zero-minimum boundary before starting the client. This keeps the gateway-client readiness boundary local and avoids adding new config, fallback behavior, or broader policy.

## User Impact

Developers can pass explicit readiness timeouts without accidentally forwarding timer values above the safe Node.js delay range to alternate readiness waiters.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: explicit gateway-client readiness timeouts are clamped to `MAX_SAFE_TIMEOUT_DELAY_MS` before the exported startup helper invokes an alternate readiness waiter, and startup still proceeds after readiness succeeds.
- Current head: `238a69ab44fe6b5ff50558f55ce462d6ae5de2de`.
- Runtime proof: a Node 22 probe imported `packages/gateway-client/src/readiness.ts` and `packages/gateway-client/src/timeouts.ts`, called `startGatewayClientWithReadinessWait(..., { timeoutMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER })`, and observed:

  ```text
  [runtime] head=238a69ab44fe6b5ff50558f55ce462d6ae5de2de
  [runtime] explicit timeout input=9007199254740991
  [runtime] waiter observed maxWaitMs=2147483647
  [runtime] safe timer maximum=2147483647
  [runtime] gateway client start invoked=1
  [runtime] readiness.ready=true
  [runtime] readiness.aborted=false
  [runtime] proof result=PASS: oversized explicit readiness timeout was clamped before startup
  ```

- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-client/src/readiness.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 2 tests passing.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the focused regression and runtime transcript both show `timeoutMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` reaches the readiness waiter as `2147483647`, the shared safe timer maximum, and the client startup path still invokes `start()` after readiness succeeds.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```





---

## Follow-up fix: mixed prose + parametrized invoke on the persist path

The initial scope covered zero-argument / self-closing invoke blocks. A separate, related leak was found afterward from a real captured session: a model turn that emits **leading visible prose** followed by a **fully-closed, parametrized** `invoke` block (namespaced or bare).

Root cause: `scrubOverCapPlainTextToolCallMessage` classifies such a turn as buffer state `"impossible"` (the leading prose means it is not a buffered tool-call prefix). When under the buffer cap it returned `undefined`, so the raw message was persisted and leaked to chat. The display path (`sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` → line-scanning `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) already strips this block, but the persist/normalize path did not, so the two diverged. Promotion cannot run for these blocks because a non-zero-offset block never parses as standalone.

Fix: before the `impossible` + under-cap `return undefined`, apply the same line-standalone `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` to each text block of the message content and return the scrubbed message, giving persist ↔ display parity. Behavior is byte-identical when nothing strips; tool execution is not widened (no auto-promotion).

Added mixed-content regression tests (bare and namespaced) asserting the persisted message carries no raw invoke XML, preserves prose up to the boundary, and does not auto-promote.

target.title: fix(agent-core): report correct JSONL entry line after blank rows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers opening a JSONL-backed agent-core session would see an incorrect invalid-entry line number when the session file contained blank JSONL rows before the malformed entry.

## Why This Change Was Made

`JsonlSessionStorage` already skips blank JSONL rows while loading sessions, so entry diagnostics should still point to the physical source line after those blanks are skipped. The parser now carries each retained row's original line number into entry validation without changing header parsing or storage semantics.

## User Impact

Developers and operators can trust invalid JSONL session diagnostics to point at the actual malformed row, making session repair and support investigation less misleading.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: JSONL session entry diagnostics preserve physical line numbers when blank rows appear before an invalid entry.
- Current-head proof at e896a3a5fcafb912d7f2424cb06f10dc06dfa822: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/agent-core/src/harness/session/jsonl-storage.test.ts` passed with 1 test file and 7 tests.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the regression test now reports `line 3 is not valid JSON` for an invalid entry that follows a blank JSONL row.

target.title: fix(computer): reject malformed numeric input before node actions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users invoking the `computer` tool through gateway-visible tool surfaces could provide malformed numeric values and have them coerced into desktop actions instead of rejected when issuing scroll, hold-key, or wait actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The computer tool now uses the existing strict numeric readers at the execution boundary for `scrollAmount` and `duration`, matching the owner-local guard pattern used by adjacent node-control numeric inputs. Valid defaults and the existing scroll clamp behavior stay intact; malformed present values fail before any node command or follow-up screenshot is invoked.

## User Impact

Malformed desktop-control numeric inputs now fail early with actionable validation errors, so invalid raw tool invocations cannot turn booleans, fractional scroll ticks, or nonnumeric durations into unintended computer-control actions.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: malformed computer numeric inputs are rejected before node invocation while valid scroll clamping remains unchanged.
- Current-head proof at `6c39afe6275c9378410dff43163d1d4efa92bfc1`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/computer-tool.test.ts` passed with 1 file and 65 tests passing.
- Branch diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.

target.title: fix(compaction): allow compaction under Bedrock aws-sdk auth with no static key
target.body:
Closes #103637
Related: #90179, #90206, #90221, #90187

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Bedrock users on `auth: "aws-sdk"` (SigV4 via the AWS SDK credential chain: EC2 instance role, SSO, STS/assumed-role, or `AWS_PROFILE`) lose their agent completely once a session grows large enough to require compaction. Every subsequent message fails with `Preflight compaction required but failed: Compaction safeguard could not resolve request credentials`, and the session logs `Compaction safeguard: no request credentials available; cancelling compaction to preserve history`. Bedrock calls otherwise work throughout the session, so the failure is surprising and has no runtime workaround.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ModelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders` intentionally returns `{ ok: true, apiKey: undefined, headers: undefined }` for `auth: "aws-sdk"` because SigV4 signing happens later at send time; the registry already treats this as valid via `allowsMissingProviderApiKey` (`aws-sdk`, `oauth`). The compaction safeguard, however, ignored that authoritative `ok: true` and re-derived failure from the absence of a static key/header, wedging compaction for every keyless request.

The safeguard now trusts the registry's `ok` signal, which already returns `ok: false` when auth genuinely cannot resolve (for example an `authHeader` provider with no key). This removes the faulty second check rather than adding a parallel path, keeping one authoritative credential-resolution boundary. A regression test covers the keyless SDK-managed auth path.

This is the same defect tracked in #90179. The earlier fix #90206 was accepted in review (cleaner `authMode` threading, `MERGEABLE`/`CLEAN`, Codex "proof: sufficient") but was closed while waiting on live real-behavior Bedrock proof from the original reporter. This PR supplies that missing proof from a live Bedrock `aws-sdk` deployment and takes the minimal form of the fix.

## User Impact

Bedrock-native users on session-based / role-based AWS auth can run long sessions again: compaction proceeds normally and messages no longer fail once the context grows. No config change, no new surface, no behavior change for API-key or `authHeader` providers.

## Evidence

Validated on a live Bedrock `aws-sdk` deployment (EC2 instance role via IMDSv2, no static key, no OpenClaw API key for Bedrock):

- Before: every Telegram/webchat message failed with `Preflight compaction required but failed: ... could not resolve request credentials for amazon-bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`, while `aws sts get-caller-identity` and a direct `bedrock-runtime converse` both succeeded with the same credentials.
- After: compaction runs and messages succeed; the `no request credentials available` log no longer appears.

Focused tests (`src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts`): 106 passed, including a new case that drives a keyless `ok: true` auth result and asserts compaction proceeds to summarization instead of cancelling.

target.title: fix: reasoning-only and empty-response retries duplicate the user message in the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model returns a reasoning-only turn (reasoning content but an empty visible completion) or a generically empty response, the embedded runner retries the turn with a visible-answer continuation. Each retry attempt currently re-persists the inbound user message, plus an empty assistant message, into the session transcript. After one exhausted episode (initial attempt plus 2 retries) the session permanently contains three copies of the same user message interleaved with three empty assistant turns.

Every later prompt build replays those duplicated, seemingly unanswered messages, and models respond by answering the same question multiple times and addressing old messages inside current turns. The effect compounds: one flaky-model hiccup degrades every subsequent turn of that session until it is reset.

The same duplicate-user-message-on-retry symptom was fixed in other retry paths in the past ([#55181](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55181), [#57880](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57880), [#61006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/61006), [#83404](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/83404)); the reasoning-only / empty-response continuation path reintroduces it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runner already has the mechanism for exactly this: `suppressNextUserMessagePersistence`, which three sibling retry paths set before re-dispatching so the next attempt does not re-persist the user turn. The reasoning-only, missing-assistant, and empty-response retry blocks `continue` the run loop without setting it. This change adds the same one-line flag assignment to those three blocks, mirroring the sibling idiom.

It also makes the two retry limits overridable via environment variables, `OPENCLAW_REASONING_ONLY_RETRY_LIMIT` and `OPENCLAW_EMPTY_RESPONSE_RETRY_LIMIT` (strict non-negative integers, parsed once at module load with the existing `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` helper, defaults unchanged at 2 and 1). Operators running models prone to reasoning-only output can tune or disable these retries without a config schema change; `0` fails fast on the first incomplete turn and surfaces the error immediately.

## User Impact

- Sessions no longer accumulate duplicate user messages during reasoning-only / empty-response retry episodes, so models stop re-answering the same message after a provider hiccup.
- No default behavior change otherwise: retries still fire with the same limits, recovery on a later attempt still works, and the incomplete-turn error still surfaces when attempts are exhausted.
- New optional env overrides for the two retry limits.

## Evidence

Live before/after from a deployment running a model that intermittently emits reasoning-only turns (`poolside/laguna-xs-2.1` via OpenRouter):

Before the fix, one exhausted episode (2 retries) left this in the session JSONL, timestamps matching the retry log lines exactly:

```
user      08:17:50  "<message>"
assistant 08:17:52  (empty)
user      08:18:00  "<message>"     <- retry 1/2 re-persisted
assistant 08:18:02  (empty)
user      08:18:05  "<message>"     <- retry 2/2 re-persisted
assistant 08:18:07  (empty)
```

After the fix (same deployment, same model, same session, identical exhausted 2-retry episode):

```
user      10:28:46  "<message>"     <- persisted exactly once
assistant 10:28:51  (empty)
assistant 10:28:59  (empty)
assistant 10:29:09  (empty)
```

The follow-up symptom (model re-answering the duplicated backlog on later turns) disappeared with it.

Tests, all included in this PR:

- New assertions prove the user message is persisted exactly once across reasoning-only and empty-response retry sequences (reverting only the `run.ts` change makes exactly these assertions fail, verified red/green).
- A limit=0 test proves the first incomplete turn goes straight to the exhausted branch: one attempt, error surfaced, no retry.
- Env parsing tests cover invalid values ("abc", "-1") falling back to defaults.
- `run.incomplete-turn.test.ts` 120/120; full embedded-agent-runner project 2301/2301; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` clean.

Note: the empty assistant message persisted by each failed attempt is pre-existing behavior and intentionally left unchanged here; it is inert (it does not trigger backlog re-answering). Happy to address it separately if wanted.

This change was developed with AI assistance and reviewed before submission.

target.title: fix: A2A handoffs can duplicate message-tool replies
target.body:
Related: #39476
Related: #91161
Related: #93293

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate visible output from an A2A handoff when the target session replies through `message(action="send")` and the waited A2A path later mistakes the resulting assistant-shaped transcript mirror for a new reply.

This was triggered by a real duplicate delivery in a local WhatsApp/Main Merid thread. Private message content is omitted, but the observed sequence was one correct requester-visible reply followed by a second visible delivery from the same A2A/source-reply flow.

This is a narrow companion to #39476. It does not replace #91161's reverse `sessions_send` guard or change the compaction replay behavior covered by #93293.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.history` can project visible message-tool mirrors and forwarded `sessions_send` rows as assistant messages. The existing waited-reply selector accepts those rows after only stripping tool messages, so A2A announce delivery can treat an already-delivered transcript artifact as a fresh model reply.

This patch keeps waited A2A reply extraction on model-authored assistant replies by rejecting inter-session input rows, raw OpenClaw delivery mirrors, projected message-tool mirrors, and Gateway-injected assistant rows. At an artifact boundary it stops instead of falling back to an older reply. It also avoids a second announce decision for same-session source replies with no valid announce target and excludes only OpenClaw's two exact incomplete-turn fallback messages from announce delivery.

No production config, secrets, channel contract, tool schema, delivery API, runtime permission, dependency, package metadata, or changelog file changes.

## User Impact

A2A handoffs that reply visibly through the message tool no longer turn already-delivered source replies or forwarded `sessions_send` transcript rows into a second visible message. Normal model-authored replies retain the existing waited-reply, ping-pong, and announce behavior.

target.title: fix: prevent silent message loss from EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError
target.body:
## Summary

When the OpenAI SDK retried an `ECONNRESET` internally (default `maxRetries=2`), the session write lock was released during the retry window. Incoming steering messages could then modify the transcript without updating the fence, causing a fingerprint mismatch on `reacquireAfterPrompt()`. The resulting `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` was caught by `model-fallback.ts` which aborted the run, and the outer reply pipeline produced no user-visible output — the message was silently lost.

## Root Cause Chain

```
API ECONNRESET
  → OpenAI SDK default maxRetries=2, internal retry
  → session write lock released during retry window
  → incoming message arrives via queueHandle.queueMessage
  → activeSession.steer writes directly (bypassing withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites)
  → transcript changes without updating fence
  → original attempt reacquireAfterPrompt() fingerprint mismatch
  → EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError thrown
  → model-fallback.ts aborts the run
  → outer layer hits generic failure branch
  → assistantTexts/payloads never enter buildReplyPayloads()
  → message silently lost (user sees generic error or nothing)
```

## Fix

Seven coordinated changes that address the bug at multiple layers:

### 1. Wrap steering in `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites` (`attempt.ts`)
Steering writes that arrive during prompt lock release now go through `withOwnedSessionTranscriptWrites`, keeping fence tracking consistent and preventing the fingerprint mismatch that triggers the takeover error.

### 2. Dedicated error handler for takeover (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `failover-error.ts`)
Added `isEmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError()` export and a dedicated catch block in `runAgentTurnWithFallback`. Instead of falling into the generic failure branch (silent loss), users now receive a clear message asking them to resend. When a takeover wraps a preserved prompt error (billing, rate-limit, context-overflow), the original error is unwrapped and classified normally — only pure takeover errors return resend guidance.

### 3. Scope SDK retry disable to embedded prompt lock path (`attempt.ts`, `attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Extracted `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` helper that wraps the session's `streamFn` with `{ maxRetries: 0, ...options }` — the `0` is a **default** that goes before the caller options spread, so `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries` (surfaced via `options.maxRetries` per the chain in `sdk.ts:360`) takes precedence when explicitly configured. Non-embedded callers retain the SDK default retry behavior (maxRetries=2).

### 4. Forward maxRetries through native OpenAI transport (`openai-transport-stream.ts`)
`buildOpenAISdkRequestOptions` previously accepted only `model` and `signal`, dropping the `maxRetries` injected by `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault`. Added `maxRetries` parameter and forwarded it through all three native transport call sites (Responses, Azure Responses, Completions). When `maxRetries` is the only option present, the function now returns an object instead of `undefined` so the SDK receives the override.

### 5. Phase tracking in `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` (`attempt.session-lock.ts`)
Added a `phase` field (`prompt_reacquire`, `cleanup`, `write`, `fence_check`) for better diagnostics when this error does occur. Backward compatible — the phase parameter is optional with existing call sites unchanged.

### 6. Restore unconfigured connection-error retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`, `embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`)
Disabling SDK retries inside the prompt-lock release window (#3) is required so an in-window retry cannot widen the takeover race — but for users who have **not** configured `settings.retry.provider.maxRetries`, it also dropped the SDK's default retry of bare connection errors (`ECONNRESET`, `socket hang up`, `Connection error.`) that carry no leading HTTP status. This is restored at the orchestrator layer, where the existing one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` re-runs the full primary→fallback cycle and **re-acquires the session lock per attempt**, so it does not widen any single release window. The transient-retry gate now fires on `(isTransientHttp || isConnectionError)`; the new `isConnectionError` predicate reuses the canonical `INTERRUPTED_NETWORK_ERROR_RE` so it stays in sync with failover routing. In-window `maxRetries:0` is unchanged. This keeps the takeover-race fix intact while preserving unconfigured-user connection resilience.

### 7. Restore unconfigured request-timeout retry at the orchestrator layer (`agent-runner-execution.ts`)
The orchestrator transient-retry restore in #6 left a symmetric gap: in addition to bare connection errors, the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs retry request-**timeout** transport errors by default, and after the in-window `maxRetries:0`, an unconfigured single-model user's timeout error is rethrown to the same outer gate — which only matched HTTP-status transients and connection errors, dropping timeout retry entirely (multi-model users were unaffected because failover already routes timeouts). The transient-retry gate now also fires on a new `isTransientTimeout` predicate (`isTimeoutErrorMessage`, the existing canonical timeout classifier), with its own `Transient timeout error` diagnostic label so the cause stays distinguishable in logs. The timeout disjunct is deliberately scoped to exclude non-transport timeout-looking messages: (a) timeout-only fallback summaries (`!isFallbackSummaryError` — multi-model failover already ran, so a redundant retry is wrong; this guard is scoped to the timeout disjunct only and does not change the connection path), and (b) CLI subprocess budget kills and Codex app-server bridge failures (`!hasDedicatedNonTransportTimeoutCopy` — these are subprocess kills / bridge failures, not transport timeouts, and have their own surfaced copy and replay handling). The one-shot `consumeTransientHttpRetry()` budget is shared, so timeout retry is bounded exactly like the connection retry. The connection-retry path semantics from #6 are unchanged. The timeout disjunct additionally excludes local non-provider runtime coordination errors (e.g. `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`, whose message reads as `session file locked (timeout ...ms)`) via the canonical `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classifier: retrying any model would hit the same local condition, so these abort the fallback chain rather than re-run as a transport timeout.

### Real session-takeover path (organic error, real transport + real fence)

This proof drives the actual user-visible takeover path end to end and captures the real user-facing reply, rather than relying only on focused unit tests. Committed as `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-session-takeover.real.test.ts`.

**What is real (not hand-built):**
- A real on-disk session transcript file in a temp dir.
- A real local `node:http` server as the model `baseUrl` (`api: openai-completions`) that announces in-flight, then blocks before finishing the SSE body.
- The real `openai-completions` transport doing real HTTP I/O.
- The real embedded prompt-lock controller + fence (`createEmbeddedAttemptSessionLockController`), wired through the real `installEmbeddedPromptRetryDefault` / `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` helpers — the exact helpers `attempt.ts` uses in production.
- The `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` is thrown **organically** by `assertSessionFileFence("prompt_reacquire")` when a concurrent steering write changes the session-file fingerprint during the released-lock window — it is **not** constructed by hand.
- The real `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` classification and the real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catch branch producing the user-facing payload.

**Mechanism (deterministic Promise handshakes, no sleeps):**
1. A real temp session file is created with one session line.
2. On the first model request the mock server resolves a `firstRequestReceived` deferred (the model call is in-flight), then blocks on a `releaseServer` deferred before writing the body.
3. `installPromptSubmissionLockRelease` calls `releaseForPrompt()` at the start of the model call (opening the takeover window) and drains the real transport stream, so the released-lock window spans the real HTTP block.
4. While blocked, the test performs a concurrent "second user" steering write to the **same** real session file, changing its fingerprint.
5. `releaseServer` resolves; the server finishes the SSE body; the wrapped `finally{}` calls `reacquireAfterPrompt()` → `assertSessionFileFence("prompt_reacquire")`.
6. The fingerprint mismatch trips the fence → `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` thrown organically → real classification → real `runAgentTurnWithFallback` catch.

target.title: fix(agents): resolveMessagePrefix now checks channel and account messagePrefix configs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `resolveMessagePrefix` helper only checked the global `messages.messagePrefix` config, ignoring channel-specific and account-specific overrides. Operators could not set per-channel or per-account message prefixes, even though `ackReaction` and `responsePrefix` both correctly cascaded through all four levels.

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/identity.ts`, `resolveMessagePrefix` accepted `configured` and `hasAllowFrom` options but lacked the `channel` and `accountId` parameters. Additionally, `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig` only passed `channel` + `accountId` to `resolveResponsePrefix`, not to `resolveMessagePrefix`. The WhatsApp caller `buildInboundLine` also omitted `accountId`, so even after the resolver supported it, account-level `messagePrefix` would never be selected in the real production path.

## Changes

### Core fix ([src/agents/identity.ts](src/agents/identity.ts))

Implement the same L1-L4 precedence cascade used by `resolveResponsePrefix` and `resolveAckReaction`:

1. **L1**: Channel account level (`channels[X].accounts[Y].messagePrefix`)
2. **L2**: Channel level (`channels[X].messagePrefix`)
3. **L3**: Global messages level (`messages.messagePrefix`) or caller-configured option
4. **L4**: `hasAllowFrom` → identity name prefix → fallback (`"[openclaw]"`)

### WhatsApp callers

- **message-line.ts**: Changed to passing `channel: "whatsapp"` + `accountId` — full L1-L4 cascade resolved internally
- **message-line.runtime.ts**: WhatsApp runtime copy updated with same L1-L4 cascade
- **process-message.ts**: Passes `params.route.accountId` through to `buildInboundLine`

### Tests

25 new tests in `identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts` covering backward compatibility, channel-level, account-level, full cascade, and `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig` integration. All existing WhatsApp inbound-line tests (23/23) pass unchanged.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` or `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with an `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. If the sandbox child's stdout or stderr pipe breaks, the codex sandbox exec server goes down.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added two stream error handlers:

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: a stdout pipe failure means the process output channel is dead. Preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`, but leave terminal notifications and finalization to the existing `child.once("close")` handler so we never report the process closed to Codex while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; losing it must not kill an otherwise healthy sandbox process — logged as a warning via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the codex sandbox exec server with an unhandled `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. Stdout failures correctly terminate the managed process through the existing close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

**Lifecycle fix:** stdout stream error now kills the child instead of calling `emitProcessClosed` directly. The close handler owns finalization uniformly.

**Focused regression (stream errors):** `processes.stream-errors.test.ts` mocks `node:child_process spawn` with an `EventEmitter` child, exercises both error paths via the production `startProcess` entry point, and asserts the lifecycle contract:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What the tests prove:**

1. **Stdout error → kill + defer to close:** `managed.failure` is set, `child.kill("SIGTERM")` is called, `managed.closed` stays `false`. The subsequent `close` event finalizes exactly once → no orphaned child.
2. **Stderr error → warn only:** `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is called, `child.kill` is never called, process stays alive — stderr is non-fatal.

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** A live Codex sandbox with a real OS pipe failure (requires resource exhaustion or a misbehaving child process). The stream error path itself is exercised exactly — spawn returns the same pipe-backed streams the production code uses, and the error events are delivered to the real handlers registered by `startProcess`.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `npx oxlint ...` — exit 0
- `npx oxfmt --check ...` — clean

target.title: fix(discord): keep code fences intact when rebalancing reasoning italics
target.body:
Closes #102911

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord reasoning messages that wrap content in `_…_` would corrupt markdown code fences and inline code when the message was split across chunks. After a chunk boundary that started with a backtick, the italics rebalancer prepended `_`, producing broken fences such as `_```python` that Discord no longer renders as code. A first-pass guard that only skipped the reopen left continuation chunks with an unmatched trailing `_` (unbalanced per-message markup).

## Why This Change Was Made

`rebalanceReasoningItalics` still closes/reopens reasoning italics so each Discord message stays independently balanced. When the next chunk starts with a backtick:

1. Do **not** prepend `_` onto the code opener (keeps ```` ``` ```` / `` `code` `` intact).
2. Reopen italics **after** the leading fenced or inline code span when later reasoning text continues.
3. Drop a lone trailing `_` on pure-code continuations (original wrap closer with no open on that chunk).
4. Only append a closing `_` when the chunk actually opened reasoning italics (avoids ```` ```_ ```` on pure-code chunks).

Regression tests assert exact second-chunk output and even `_` counts, not only “does not start with `_``` `”.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning/thinking replies that contain code blocks or inline code no longer break markdown fences at chunk boundaries, and each chunk keeps balanced reasoning italics when text continues after code.

## Evidence

### Focused tests
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

### Production-path harness (`chunkDiscordText` → `rebalanceReasoningItalics`)

**Current main (before):**
```
chunks=2
chunk[1] starts with "_```python\nx\n```_"
BUG_CONFIRMED=true
```

**This patch:**
```
===fence===
chunk[1] = "```python\nprint(1)\n```"   # balanced (0 _), fence intact
===inline===
chunk[1] = "`inline_code_token`\n_10. after_"   # reopen after code; even _
===fence+text===
chunk[1] = "```python\nprint(1)\n```\n_more reasoning_"   # reopen after fence
===control-normal===
chunks reopen with leading "_" as before
```

### Changed-lane gates
```
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs  # PASS
pnpm test:changed  # PASS (extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts, 20 tests)
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Discord reasoning-italics rebalance protects backtick-leading openers and keeps per-message `_` balance (reopen after code, or strip lone closer on pure-code chunks).
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout, Node 24; production helper `chunkDiscordText` (same path used by Discord send/outbound). Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).
- Current-main contrast: with `maxLines: 10` and a 9-line reasoning body ending in a fenced block, the second chunk began with `_```python`, which breaks Discord fence parsing; skip-only reopen left ` ```…```_ ` with an unmatched closer.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node --import tsx` harness calling `chunkDiscordText` with fence, inline, fence+text, and normal reopen fixtures
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts`
  3. `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs`
  4. `pnpm test:changed`
- Evidence after fix: fence-only second chunk is exact ` ```python\nprint(1)\n``` ` (no leading/trailing `_`); inline second chunk is `` `inline_code_token`\n_10. after_ ``; fence+text reopens after the fence; every fixture has even `_` counts; 20/20 tests green including three code-boundary cases with exact-output asserts.
- Control check: normal multi-chunk reasoning still reopens with leading `_` on non-code continuations; existing balance tests still pass.
- Observed result after fix: code fences/inline code at chunk boundaries stay intact and each emitted message remains delimiter-balanced.
- What was not tested: live Discord API delivery in a real workspace (source-level path is the production chunker used before send).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Implementation, tests, and proof were verified against current main and the ClawSweeper review on #103166 (balance backtick-leading continuation; exact-output/delimiter-balance asserts).

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox exec-server subprocesses (both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream `error` events, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox child process exits or its pipes break, the Node stream layer emits `error` on the child's stdout/stderr `Readable` streams. With no `error` listener attached, Node re-throws the event, which bubbles into a process-fatal unhandled error and terminates the exec-server bridge. Both subprocess owners — `processes.ts` (process RPC) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP) — had this gap.

The fix attaches a no-op `error` listener on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` at each spawn point, mirroring the repo-standard pattern already used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The process `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle and finalization.

Rebased onto current `main`; resolved a conflict with #103617 (defer sandbox cleanup until process close), which restructured both spawn sites into a `try/catch`. The no-op listeners are now attached after the guarded spawn, preserving that ownership.

## User Impact

The Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess output pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Production change (both subprocess owners):**

- `processes.ts` — after the guarded `spawn`, before the `data` listeners:
  ```ts
  const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
  child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
  child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
  ```
- `http.ts` — identical guard after the guarded `spawn` in `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest`.

**Mutation-sensitive regression test** (`sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts`): it spies on `node:child_process` `spawn` to capture the real spawned child, then **deterministically emits `error` on the real `child.stdout` and `child.stderr`** for both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP path. It asserts each stream carries an `error` listener, that emitting the error does not throw, that the WebSocket bridge stays `OPEN`, and (process path) that the bridge still runs follow-up work.

Because emitting `error` on a stream with no `error` listener throws synchronously, removing either production listener makes the test fail — proving the test protects the exact fixed path.

**Diagnostic proof — fix present vs. removed:**

With the fix in place:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

With **both** `child.stdout.on("error", …)` / `child.stderr.on("error", …)` removed from `processes.ts` and `http.ts` (mutation), the same test fails on the real emitted stream errors:

```text
 FAIL  sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts > process bridge suppresses stdout/stderr errors and keeps serving
 AssertionError: process stdout has no error listener: expected 0 to be greater than 0
 FAIL  sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts > streaming HTTP bridge suppresses stdout/stderr errors after headers
 AssertionError: http stdout has no error listener: expected 0 to be greater than 0
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

**Sibling exec-server suites still green after the rebase:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs sandbox-exec-server.{http,lifecycle,json-rpc}.test.ts sandbox-exec-server.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

The same no-op `error` listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.
