target.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Nextcloud Talk outbound adapter had no `sanitizeText` hook. Core delivery (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts:889-896`) only runs the per-channel assistant-text sanitizer when the adapter provides one; without it, internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding is delivered verbatim to the chat. Users see raw banners like `⚠️ 🛠️ `exec (agent)`` failed` and raw `<tool_call>`/`<function_response>` XML in their Nextcloud Talk messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** the outbound adapter omits the `sanitizeText` hook that strips internal runtime scaffolding before delivery.
- **Fix:** add `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` to the outbound base adapter — the identical one-line hook already shipped to 13 sibling channels: mattermost (#98693), feishu (#98705), twitch (#103109), signal (#97360), slack (#97367), matrix (#97372), irc (#97214), telegram, googlechat (#90684), qqbot (#90132), discord, whatsapp (#71830), and sms.
- The hook runs in core delivery before chunk planning, so the markdown chunker only ever sees sanitized text.

## User Impact

Internal tool-trace banners and leaked XML scaffolding no longer reach Nextcloud Talk users. Ordinary assistant prose is preserved unchanged.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Sibling fixes: #103109, #98693, #98705.

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node --import tsx` runtime verification calling the **patched adapter hook** `nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText` (the exact hook added by this PR) on the exact PR head:

```
sanitizeText hook exists: true
[PASS] tool-trace banner: "Done."
[PASS] xml tool-call: "Meeting notes sent."
[PASS] plain prose: "The agenda has 3 open action items."
```

This calls the real `nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText` (resolved from `{ base: { sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text) } }` via `resolveChatChannelOutbound`), proving the patched Nextcloud Talk adapter routes assistant text through the sanitizer before delivery.

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | Nextcloud Talk outbound delivers internal tool-trace scaffolding verbatim (no sanitizeText hook). |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22; the patched adapter hook invoked on the exact PR head (fad7fab8f17b). |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx` script that imports `nextcloudTalkPlugin` and calls `outbound.sanitizeText` directly, plus colocated vitest `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/<channel>/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts`. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal output above: the patched adapter hook strips banners, XML tool-call scaffolding, while preserving ordinary prose. |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | The channel outbound hook removes tool-trace scaffolding; ordinary text unchanged. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live channel server delivery (no server in this env); the adapter hook itself is exercised directly on the real plugin object. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/channel.core.test.ts
✓ extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/channel.core.test.ts (3 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

New `outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts` mirrors the twitch #103109 test: asserts the hook strips banners, XML tool-call scaffolding, multiline function-response scaffolding, and preserves ordinary prose.

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only the Nextcloud Talk outbound sanitizeText hook.
- [x] No config/env/default surface change.
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change (reuses an already-exported SDK helper).
- [x] Backward compatible — only internal scaffolding is removed; user-visible prose is unchanged.
- [x] No new deps (helper already in the SDK barrel).
- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

- [x] Allow edits by maintainers

---

Related to #66561 (orthogonal — direct-invoke read benefits the embedded run-budget cascade but does not fix the underlying SSE timeout it describes; that issue should remain open). Narrow first landing of the broader direct-invoke umbrella tracked in #37131.

## Summary

Wire the `read` coding tool into the gateway direct-invoke surfaces (HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND SDK RPC `tools.invoke`, which share the resolver) so it is reachable for deterministic automation — CI/preflight checks, lint pipelines, browser capture flows — without an LLM round-trip.

**This PR is the redesigned narrow read-only landing.** Rebased onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. The exposure of `read` is now behind **triple-key gating** so neither the existing `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` knob nor the new opt-in silently grants host-FS read, and a non-owner trusted-proxy caller can never reach it.

## Triple-key gating (addresses ClawSweeper [P1] + owner hardening)

To reach `read` on the direct-invoke surface, ALL THREE must hold:

| Key | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` | Lifts `read` from `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY` (now extended with `"read"`). Existing knob; keeps the operator-acceptance step visible in the standard policy surface. | not present |
| `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead: true` | **NEW.** Distinct surface-specific opt-in. Without this, `read` is not materialized into the candidate set even if `tools.allow` includes it. | `false` (omitted) |
| `senderIsOwner === true` | **NEW owner gate.** Host-filesystem read is materialized only for an owner/admin sender. A trusted-proxy `operator.write` caller is denied even with both config keys set. | n/a (per-request) |

**Any key alone (or any two) leaves `read` unreachable.** Old configs that already contain `allow: ["read"]` for unrelated reasons (e.g. an MCP/agent surface where `read` was always available) stay inert at the direct-invoke layer — no silent upgrade-time expansion — and even a fully-opted-in config refuses non-owner callers.

| `tools.allow` ⊇ `"read"` | `directInvoke.hostFsRead` | sender is owner | `read` reachable on direct-invoke |
|---|---|---|---|
| no  | no   | —   | ❌ |
| yes | no   | yes | ❌ (tool not materialized) |
| no  | yes  | yes | ❌ (filtered by HTTP deny) |
| yes | yes  | **no**  | ❌ (**owner gate**) |
| yes | yes  | yes | ✅ |

## Scope

- **Read-only.** Mutating coding primitives (`write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` / `exec` / `process`) are NOT exposed by this PR.
- **Both surfaces.** Gating applies to HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND the SDK-facing JSON-RPC `tools.invoke` (they share `resolveGatewayScopedTools`).
- **MCP loopback unaffected.** `surface === "loopback"` is not gated.
- **Hook-bypass safe.** Uses new `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export (module-private Symbol marker, not reachable from typed SDK params) so HTTP-surface tools aren't double-wrapped — `handleToolsInvokeHttp` already runs `runBeforeToolCallHook` itself before dispatch.

## Files changed

- `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` — `SKIP_BEFORE_TOOL_CALL_HOOK` symbol + `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export
- `src/config/types.gateway.ts` — `GatewayToolsConfig.directInvoke: GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` field (new type)
- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` — `"read"` added to `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY`
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` — triple-key gated materialization of `read` into the candidate set (`tools.allow` ∋ read AND `directInvoke.hostFsRead` AND `senderIsOwner`)
- `src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.test.ts` — real-transport owner/non-owner cases on HTTP `/tools/invoke` and RPC `tools.invoke`
- `src/security/audit-gateway-config.ts` — `gateway.tools_invoke_http.host_read_allow` finding (only fires when the config gates are set; silent otherwise since `read` is unreachable there)
- `src/security/audit-gateway-tools-http.test.ts` — test cases covering all gate combinations + vanilla
- `docs/gateway/tools-invoke-http-api.md` — operator-facing opt-in docs with config example + truth table
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — `+1` surface-budget bump (4 dimensions) to admit the single new `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` public config type; no runtime impact

## Why a redesigned commit history (not a rebase of the prior 10)

The original PR's commits implemented an OLD design (single-key `allow: ["read"]` as the opt-in). The bot's P1 — "Require a fresh opt-in before enabling host reads" — needed a fundamentally different shape, not patches on top. Plus the prior commits referenced `src/agents/pi-tools.ts` which has been renamed to `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` upstream. The branch was reset onto upstream and the redesign written cleanly, then rebased again onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. Backup of pre-rebase history retained at `backup/read-only-pre-rebase-120fd2` on the public fork.

The final commit (`chore(plugin-sdk): bump surface budgets +1 for GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns`) is the only behavioural-neutral addition: the new public config type `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` adds exactly one top-level export, which the `plugin-sdk-surface-report --check` budget ratchet (run by `checks-node-core-fast`) counts against four dimensions (`config-types`, public exports, public function exports, public deprecated exports — the monolithic `config-types` entrypoint is `@deprecated`). Each budget constant is bumped `+1` to admit the single new type; no runtime code is touched by that commit, so the live proof and `dist/` are identical with or without it.

---

## Real behavior proof

> **Head `5ca72af1ba`** — rebased onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38` (the prior base `120fd2f702` was 28 commits stale; upstream `1c0b38f960 fix(sdk): refresh plugin surface baselines` is included in the new base). Re-built and re-proven from scratch in docker at this exact head. CI verified locally before push (in `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64): oxlint (3 shards, 0/0), `tsgo:core` (0), `tsgo:test` / `check:test-types` (0), `plugin-sdk-surface-report` vitest (4/4), and the 3 PR-touched test files 143/143 (7 file-projects).

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Expose the `read` coding tool over Gateway direct-invoke surfaces (HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND SDK RPC `tools.invoke`, which share the resolver) for deterministic automation, gated behind `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` + the NEW `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead: true` opt-in + an owner gate. Addresses ClawSweeper [P1] (legacy single-key config must NOT silently grant host-FS read on upgrade) and adds owner-only enforcement so a non-owner trusted-proxy caller is refused even when both config keys are set.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** built `dist/` + `packages/sdk/dist/` inside the container at head `5ca72af1ba`, then `PROOF_HEAD=5ca72af1bab7ad9d06136c47861c5d087f4d5a71 bash .proof-85664.sh` — runs a live gateway per case over a real socket. 6 cases: HTTP trusted-proxy surface (owner=`operator.admin`, non-owner=`operator.write`) for cases 1–5; SDK `GatewayClientTransport` shared-secret bearer (= owner) for case 6.

**Real environment tested:** built fresh from head `5ca72af1bab7ad9d06136c47861c5d087f4d5a71` inside `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64-native container (pnpm v11.2.2, linux-arm64 packages in a named volume). Gateway started per case via `openclaw gateway run`; each case dispatched via real HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` and (case 6) the SDK `GatewayClientTransport` WebSocket `oc.tools.invoke(...)`. Unit tests in the same container: 143/143 passing (7 files), including the real-transport owner/non-owner cases on the `gateway-server` and `gateway-client` projects.

**Evidence after fix (terminal capture, head `5ca72af1ba`):** from the `node:22-bookworm-slim` (linux/arm64) container:

```
=== HEAD: 5ca72af1bab7 ===

### LIVE PROOF (HTTP trusted-proxy surface) ###

--- 1 R-OWNER-ENABLED   (allow=[read] hostFsRead=true, operator.admin) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 200 {"ok":true,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"PROOF READ SENTINEL at 5ca72af1bab7\\n"}]}}
--- 2 R-NONOWNER-DENIED (allow=[read] hostFsRead=true, operator.write) ---
  [HTTP operator.write] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: read"}}

--- 3 R-DENIED-no-opt-in (allow=[read] hostFsRead=false, operator.admin) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: read"}}

--- 4 R-DENIED-no-allow  (allow=[] hostFsRead=true, operator.admin) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: read"}}

--- 5 WRITE-still-denied (allow=[write] hostFsRead=true, operator.admin, tool=write) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: write"}}

### LIVE PROOF (SDK token surface — shared-secret bearer = owner) ###

--- 6 SDK-OWNER-ENABLED (allow=[read] hostFsRead=true, token bearer) ---
  [SDK token] {"ok":true,"toolName":"read","output":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"PROOF READ SENTINEL at 5ca72af1bab7\\n"}]},"source":"core"}

=== PROOF COMPLETE: HEAD=5ca72af1bab7 ===
=== UNIT TESTS ===
 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  143 passed (143)
```

**Observed result after fix (head `5ca72af1ba`):**
- **Case 1 R-OWNER-ENABLED** — all three keys satisfied (owner `operator.admin`, both config keys) → HTTP 200 with the actual sentinel file content.
- **Case 2 R-NONOWNER-DENIED** — both config keys set but caller is `operator.write` (non-owner) → 404. **This is the owner gate working**: a trusted-proxy non-owner cannot reach host read even with the opt-in fully enabled.
- **Case 3 R-DENIED-no-opt-in** — `allow:["read"]` but `hostFsRead:false`, owner → 404 (P1 fix: legacy config stays inert).
- **Case 4 R-DENIED-no-allow** — `hostFsRead:true` but `allow:[]`, owner → 404 (both config keys required).
- **Case 5 WRITE-still-denied** — `allow:["write"]`, `hostFsRead:true`, owner, tool=`write` → 404 (read-only scope confirmed; the opt-in does not leak to mutating tools).
- **Case 6 SDK-OWNER-ENABLED** — SDK RPC `tools.invoke` over a shared-secret bearer (always owner) with both config keys → `ok:true`, `source:"core"`, same sentinel content. Confirms the SDK surface shares the resolver and the same gate.

**What was not tested:** Write/edit/exec/process are out of scope for this read-only PR (write/edit covered by #63919). `apply_patch` is in the deny list, not yet factory-produced. SDK over trusted-proxy WS additionally requires device pairing ("device identity required"), so the SDK non-owner path is covered by the shared `gateway-client` unit test rather than a live SDK socket; the resolver under test is identical across surfaces.

## Docs discoverability

Addresses ClawSweeper's [P2]: "Document the host-FS read opt-in everywhere."

- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — FIELD_HELP entries for `gateway.tools.directInvoke` and `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead`.
- `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` — paragraph describing the gating + audit warning hookup.
- `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` — catalog row for `gateway.tools_invoke_http.host_read_allow` with severity, criteria, and config-key references.

So operators using config help/lookup or security-audit docs can discover this security-sensitive opt-in and warning.

target.title: fix(extensions/anthropic): preserve migrated model entries when inherited keys shadow converted refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where adopting Claude CLI auth could silently drop a model'\''s custom settings (aliases, parameters, etc.) when the config'\''s `models` map was created with an inherited property matching the converted Anthropic ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteModelEntryMap` used `converted in next` to decide whether to copy the legacy `claude-cli/*` entry to its Anthropic equivalent. The `in` operator follows the prototype chain, so an inherited key matching `converted` was treated as an existing own entry. The migration then skipped the copy and deleted the original `claude-cli/*` key, losing the user'\''s model configuration.

Switching to `Object.hasOwn(next, converted)` makes the check operate on own properties only, matching the fix in #103373 for the Anthropic default-allowlist seeding path.

## User Impact

Users with prototype-bearing or otherwise inherited `models` maps no longer lose per-model aliases or other metadata when migrating to Claude CLI-backed Anthropic refs.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that constructs a `models` object with an inherited `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` key and verifies the migrated `claude-cli/claude-opus-4-7` entry is written as an own property.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts` passes (16/16).
- `pnpm oxfmt` and `pnpm oxlint` pass on the changed files.

target.title: fix(cron): preserve table Unicode boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep cron table truncation UTF-16 safe at the existing column widths.
- Add a boundary regression for an astral Unicode character in the name column.
- Exercise the actual `openclaw cron add` and `openclaw cron list --all` CLI commands over an authenticated loopback Gateway protocol endpoint.

## What Problem This Solves

`printCronList()` is the source-of-truth human-table formatter for jobs returned by `cron list`. Its local `truncate()` helper uses fixed UTF-16 code-unit `slice()` calls. The 24-character Name column reserves three characters for `...`, so a name of `x × 20 + 🚀 + tail` splits the rocket at its 21-code-unit prefix boundary. Writing that lone high surrogate to stdout encodes it as U+FFFD.

Current `origin/main` still contains the raw truncation:

```text
origin/main=7fe004d85251327db004be130699e69216fda09c
src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts:358
return `${value.slice(0, width - 3)}...`;
```

## User Impact

A cron job whose display name crosses a fixed table-column boundary at an astral Unicode character can render as a replacement glyph in `openclaw cron list`. The table remains the same width and keeps the existing ASCII ellipsis, but now preserves valid Unicode.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #102969.

Gap this fills: #102969 established the repository-safe handling for fixed-width UTF-16 presentation boundaries, while the cron CLI table retained two raw `slice()` branches.

Consistency: the patch reuses the existing core `truncateUtf16Safe` helper, preserving the table formatter's existing code-unit width contract instead of defining a new truncation policy.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

The current open-PR scan found no PR changing `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts` or `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts` for this Unicode-boundary condition.

```json
[]
```

This patch is limited to the cron table formatter and its colocated regression test.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Prevents a malformed replacement glyph in a user-visible cron CLI table without changing existing column widths or ordinary ASCII truncation.
- **Risk labels considered:** None.
- **Risk explanation:** At a surrogate boundary, the helper may retain one fewer UTF-16 code unit than raw `slice()` so that it never emits an unpaired surrogate.
- **Why acceptable:** The formatter retains its current width tests, `...` suffix, padding, columns, gateway response contract, and job scheduling behavior. Only an invalid boundary moves backward by one code unit.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the formatting boundary: the repository helper is already canonical, the focused regression passes, and actual CLI commands traverse the authenticated Gateway client protocol before rendering the observed table.
- **Patch quality notes:** The production diff replaces only the two raw truncation branches, including the existing `width <= 3` branch. No formatter refactor or protocol change is included.
- **Target test file:** `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts` checks the 24-column Name boundary through `printCronList()`.
- **Root cause:** The source-of-truth `truncate()` helper counts UTF-16 code units with raw `slice()`. Both branches can end a rendered cell immediately after a high surrogate when a valid `CronJob` name contains an astral character at the fixed boundary.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Every truncated cron table cell is routed through this helper before padding and stdout rendering. Reusing the shared UTF-16-safe slice at that ownership point prevents malformed output for Name, Declaration, Delivery, Agent ID, Owner, Model, and narrow-width cells rather than trying to repair encoded output downstream.
- **What did NOT change:** No cron schema/type, job creation semantics, persistence, scheduler, run behavior, Gateway authorization, RPC method payload, table column width, terminal styling, or JSON output changed; unrelated cron behavior is out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts` owns the human-table rendering contract. `CronJob` remains owned by the cron domain and its `cron.list` Gateway response; the CLI continues to consume that runtime object and only applies display formatting at its existing boundary.
- **Scenario locked in:** A disabled job named `x × 20 + 🚀 + tail` exceeds the 24-character Name column, causing the old 21-character pre-ellipsis prefix to cut inside the rocket surrogate pair.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** Substituting `truncateUtf16Safe` in both existing branches preserves every caller and width budget while centralizing valid-Unicode enforcement where all table cells are already truncated.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `openclaw cron list --all` no longer renders U+FFFD when the existing Name column boundary bisects an astral Unicode character.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User `openclaw cron add --name` input → Commander option parsing and cron-add parameter normalization → `cron.add` Gateway RPC → stored/runtime `CronJob` → `cron.list` Gateway RPC response → `registerCronListCommand()` → `printCronList()` → `truncate()` → terminal stdout effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** The proof runs the actual source CLI twice against a loopback WebSocket endpoint: the client receives `connect.challenge`, sends its explicit token in `connect`, then performs real `cron.add`, `cron.status`, and `cron.list` request/response frames before the list command renders stdout.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`'s `truncateUtf16Safe`; no provider, credential, scheduling, or configuration constraint changed.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 22, source `openclaw` CLI, isolated temporary `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and a `127.0.0.1` token-authenticated WebSocket server that implements the repository's exact minimal Gateway handshake and RPC response envelopes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts`; then `bash cron-cli-protocol-e2e-after.sh`, which starts the evidence-only loopback endpoint and invokes source `openclaw cron add --disabled --at +1h --name 'x × 20 + 🚀 + tail'` followed by source `openclaw cron list --all`.
- **Evidence after fix:** `cron-regression-test.txt` records 37 passing focused tests. `cron-cli-protocol-e2e-after.txt` records actual CLI add/list output with `xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...`, `hasLoneHighSurrogate: false`, `hasReplacementCharacter: false`, and `safeTruncation: true`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The rendered Name cell keeps the 20-character prefix plus `...`; it contains neither an unpaired high surrogate nor U+FFFD.
- **What was not tested:** A complete production Gateway process could not be used in this environment: its checked-out `dist` is missing a referenced chunk and a source-Gateway attempt did not listen before the bounded readiness deadline. The loopback endpoint is deliberately limited to the repository's client handshake and `cron.add`/`cron.list`/`cron.status` response contract; it does not claim to prove Gateway cron persistence or scheduler execution.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

```text
BEFORE (unmodified origin/main through the same CLI/protocol path)
Name column: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx�...
UTF-8 result: hasReplacementCharacter=true, safeTruncation=false

AFTER (current patch through the same CLI/protocol path)
Name column: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...
UTF-8 result: hasLoneHighSurrogate=false, hasReplacementCharacter=false, safeTruncation=true
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Run `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts`.
- Use `x × 20 + 🚀 + tail` to place the fixed 21-code-unit pre-ellipsis boundary inside the rocket.
- Confirm the source CLI completes authenticated `cron add` and `cron list --all` WebSocket RPC calls and its final table contains the safe prefix, no unpaired surrogate, and no U+FFFD.
- Leave existing scheduling, status, delivery preview, and regular table-rendering tests unchanged.

## Risk / Compatibility

No public API, configuration, Gateway RPC payload, job storage, scheduler behavior, table columns, or ASCII ellipsis behavior changes. At the one invalid UTF-16 boundary, the displayed prefix can be one code unit shorter so that the output remains valid Unicode.

## What was not changed

No cron scheduler configuration, Gateway server method, persistent store, job lifecycle, delivery, agent routing, terminal color policy, or JSON-format output was modified.

## Root Cause

Raw `String.prototype.slice()` measures UTF-16 code units rather than Unicode code points. The cron CLI's shared fixed-width table formatter used it both for narrow widths and the `width - 3` prefix before its ellipsis. A valid astral character at the boundary became a lone high surrogate, which Node encoded to U+FFFD when writing the rendered table. Reusing the established safe helper preserves the bounded-table contract at the formatter that owns this display transformation.

target.title: feat(gateway): add cooperative host suspension
target.body:
Partially addresses #86876.

## What Problem This Solves

External hosting controllers had no atomic way to verify that a Gateway had stopped accepting new tracked user work and was idle before freezing or snapshotting its process.

A read-only preflight can race with a new RPC, session turn, cron tick, HTTP request, or detached persistence/delivery task. Restart draining is one-way, so it cannot safely represent an abandoned or reversible host snapshot operation.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a host-neutral Gateway contract instead of a platform-specific API:

- `gateway.suspend.prepare`
- `gateway.suspend.status`
- `gateway.suspend.resume`

`prepare` closes process-wide root, session, and command admission; pauses automatic cron scheduling; and synchronously inspects tracked active work. It returns `ready` only when the snapshot is idle. If work is active, it restores scheduling and admission before returning `busy`.

A ready lease lasts two minutes, can be renewed with the same stable `requestId`, auto-resumes on expiry, and requires the matching `suspensionId` for explicit resume. Scheduler-resume failures remain fail-closed and retryable. Restart signaling shares the same admission state, preventing a signal from racing a ready lease or reopening work during restart drain.

The generic fence lives in core. The Admin HTTP plugin exposes the same RPC methods as an alternate authenticated control path. The protocol change is additive and introduces no new config or environment variable.

This is complementary to the durable queue work in #51620 and #82572: the queue preserves accepted work, while this contract creates a bounded cooperative idle window for host snapshots.

## User Impact

Host controllers can now coordinate a bounded idle window:

1. Fence host-controlled ingress.
2. Call `gateway.suspend.prepare`.
3. Retry a `busy` result while leaving the process running.
4. Freeze or snapshot before `expiresAtMs` after a `ready` result.
5. Call `gateway.suspend.resume` after thaw or abandonment.

While prepared, new WebSocket handshakes are rejected; existing connections can call only suspension control methods; other RPCs return retryable `UNAVAILABLE`; automatic cron ticks remain paused; built-in HTTP user-work routes return `503`; `/healthz` remains live; and `/readyz` reports not ready. A retained authenticated WebSocket or pre-enabled Admin HTTP RPC route is required for explicit resume.

This is a cooperative tracked-work fence, not general process quiescence. It does not persist incoming messages, stop third-party channel transports, fence external ingress, or prove arbitrary plugin/background work idle. The host remains responsible for fencing ingress and consistently freezing or snapshotting the full process tree and filesystem. If the control connection is lost, admission reopens when the lease expires.

## Evidence

- Black-box Gateway behavior on Blacksmith Testbox: idle prepare/resume, `cron.add` accepted while running, retryable `UNAVAILABLE` while prepared, mismatched resume kept the fence closed, matching resume reopened work, and repeated resume returned `resumed: false`.
- Real probe regression: `/healthz` stays `200`, `/readyz` becomes `503` during a prepared lease, and matching resume restores `200`.
- Focused protocol, client, RPC, admission, probe, cron, restart, and coordinator suites: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx5pjwe2kbstf4005a2cxm7g`, 388 tests passed; [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29084016457).
- Restart-race follow-up regressions: 527 tests passed with the repository's narrow local Vitest fallback after two fresh Testboxes were shut down during checkout before executing code; failed infrastructure runs [29084465763](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29084465763) and [29084541829](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29084541829).
- Canonical build: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx5phrr48972e9gw7586wvch`; [Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29083982557). Public Plugin SDK declarations are 4,477,008/5,000,000 bytes, and the new protocol-registry reachability guard passes.
- Fresh high-reasoning review found two restart races; both were fixed with regressions. The follow-up review reports no accepted/actionable findings.

Generated TypeBox protocol schemas, Swift client models, and the docs map are current and idempotent after rebasing onto current `main`.

target.title: add whatsapp outbound token diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can look successful when WhatsApp Web accepts a proactive 1:1 send but does not actually deliver it to a cold contact.

That is bad because the agent may believe a message was sent while the recipient never receives it. This PR makes that state easier to diagnose and avoids known PN/LID routing misses before send.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped update this branch and evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

WhatsApp/Baileys now stores and routes many direct contacts through LID JIDs. The old outbound path could trust stale local PN-to-LID files or miss the Baileys LID lookup path entirely.

This update keeps the fix local to the WhatsApp plugin:

- resolve phone-number targets through Baileys `getLIDForPN(...)` first
- fall back to a full-PN-JID USync lookup when needed
- refresh stale forward and reverse LID mapping files
- check trusted-contact token state for direct 1:1 sends
- keep token diagnostics best-effort during reconnect windows
- forward the needed socket query and diagnostic methods through the timeout adapter

## User Impact

Proactive WhatsApp sends should be less likely to go to a sender-only or wrong PN/LID target when Baileys already knows the contact LID.

When WhatsApp has an active reachout timelock and no trusted-contact token, OpenClaw now fails before `sendMessage` with a clearer error instead of letting the send look accepted but invisible.

If the socket is reconnecting, the new diagnostics do not block the existing send retry path.

## Evidence

Current head: `4bd3b8fd79cd745c7b243760e4504e3ab7365689`

Focused validation after rebasing on current `origin/main`:

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-whatsapp.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/socket-timing.test.ts

```text

The focused tests cover:

- existing authDir PN-to-LID mapping is used for sendMessage
- Baileys `getLIDForPN(...)` is preferred before direct USync

target.title: fix(gateway): use truncateUtf16Safe for voice-wake trigger truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeVoiceWakeTriggers()` in `src/gateway/server-utils.ts` truncates user-configured voice wake trigger phrases to 64 characters with naive `.slice(0, 64)`. Voice wake triggers are user-configurable text strings that may contain emoji or non-BMP characters. A `.slice(0, 64)` at a surrogate pair boundary produces a lone high surrogate (0xD83D), which corrupts the trigger text sent to the speech recognition service.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.slice(0, 64)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(value, 64)` — the standard UTF-16-safe truncation helper already used across the gateway module (same pattern as assistant-identity.ts, chat-display-projection.ts, ws-log.ts).

## User Impact

Voice wake trigger phrases containing emoji or CJK supplementary characters near the 64-char limit now remain valid UTF-16, without lone surrogates that could break downstream speech recognition or display.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value cron.sessionRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `cron.sessionRetention: "0h"` (or `"0d"`, `"0ms"`) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. Unlike `heartbeat.every` — where `"0m"` is the documented disable sentinel with a runtime `ms <= 0` guard in `resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` — `cron.sessionRetention` uses `false` (boolean) to disable and `resolveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` directly with no guard. `sweepCronRunSessions` then computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all cron run sessions for immediate deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `superRefine` only checks whether `parseDurationMs` throws — treating any non-throwing return value (including `0`) as valid. `parseDurationMs` itself returns `0` for zero inputs (not an error), and `resolveRetentionMs` does not defend against it. The positivity gate belongs in schema validation where config-level diagnostics surface the misconfiguration before runtime damage.

target.title: fix: prevent Web Push broadcasts from spiking outbound requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators broadcasting a Web Push notification to many browser or device subscriptions would open every outbound HTTPS push request at once. Large subscription sets could therefore create an avoidable burst of sockets, encryption work, and upstream requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The broadcast now schedules subscription sends through the shared bounded-concurrency worker with a limit of 12 while preserving input order and best-effort per-subscription results. VAPID details are passed per send so overlapping bounded broadcasts cannot overwrite each other's identity, and expired subscriptions are removed in one compare-before-clear state update without deleting a registration refreshed while its old send was in flight.

## User Impact

Web Push broadcasts continue attempting every subscription and cleaning up 404/410 endpoints, but peak outbound send concurrency is now capped. This reduces resource spikes for users with many browser, device, or team subscriptions without adding configuration or changing the payload/API surface.

## Evidence

- Focused local Vitest run of `src/infra/push-web.test.ts`: **14 tests passed**. Coverage includes the 12-send ceiling, complete fan-out, overlapping broadcasts with distinct VAPID identities, compare-before-clear during a subscription refresh, cleanup persistence failure, and mixed 201/404/410 results. The suite also passed with all three VAPID environment variables pre-populated to verify test isolation.
- Local live transport proof invoked the production `broadcastWebPush()` path with 25 generated browser subscriptions and a real local HTTPS push-service fixture. `web-push` performed payload encryption and issued 25 HTTPS requests; the observed peak was **12** concurrent requests. The fixture returned 23×201, 1×410, and 1×404; the broadcast returned all 25 results and persisted 23 subscriptions after cleanup. A one-day self-signed fixture certificate was used with TLS verification disabled only for this local loopback proof.
- `oxfmt --check src/infra/push-web.ts src/infra/push-web.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

AI-assisted: implementation and review were performed with coding agents. A local `codex review --base origin/main` attempt could not start because the configured provider credential (`MYAPI_API_KEY`) is unavailable; independent read-only review found no remaining actionable issues.

target.title: fix(acp): handle Gateway replace deltas in translator, not byte-offset slices
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The ACP translator in `src/acp/translator.ts` assumes Gateway assistant text only ever grows as an append-only prefix. When the model revises in-progress output so the new text is **not** a prefix extension, the translator slices the new full text at the old byte length. This produces corrupted output:

- **Divergent revision** "Hello world" → "Goodbye world": the delta becomes `"Goodbye world".slice(11)` = `"d"`, so the ACP client renders "Hello world" + "d" = "Hello worldd" — a stale prefix with a nonsensical tail.
- **Shorter revision** "Hello world!" → "Hi": `"Hi".length (2) <= sentSoFar (12)` returns early, so the client never sees "Hi" and stays stuck on the stale longer text.

The Gateway already signals non-append revisions via `replace: true` on the chat event payload (per `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/logs-chat.ts:150`), but the translator ignored it entirely.

Fixes #102322

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is two-fold:

1. `handleChatEvent` never passed the `replace` flag from `payload.replace` into `handleDeltaEvent`.
2. `handleDeltaEvent` used `pending.sentTextLength` / `pending.sentThoughtLength` to compute a byte-offset slice (`fullText.slice(sentSoFar)`), which is only correct for strict append-only frames.

**Fix** (2 files, +174/-3 lines):

- `src/acp/translator.ts`: Extract `replace` from the payload (delta frames only) and pass it to `handleDeltaEvent`. When `replace` is true, reset sentLength tracking to 0 so the full revised text (and thought) is emitted.
- `src/acp/translator.stop-reason.test.ts`: 2 regression tests covering divergent revision and shorter revision scenarios.

The `replace` flag is only used for delta frames (`state === "delta"`); final frames continue to use the existing tracking (after a replace delta, sentLength matches the revised text, so the final frame's delta produces an empty slice — no duplicate emission).

## Evidence

All 105 ACP test files pass (828 tests, zero failures or regressions):

```
$ npx vitest run src/acp/ --no-coverage

 Test Files  105 passed (105)
      Tests  828 passed (828)
   Start at  16:41:14
   Duration  55.29s
```

New regression tests specifically exercise the two failure modes:

```
$ npx vitest run src/acp/translator.stop-reason.test.ts --no-coverage

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
   Start at  16:36:01
   Duration  1.35s
```

**"emits the full revised text on a replace delta, not a byte-offset slice"**
- Sends append delta "Hello world", then replace delta "Goodbye world"
- Asserts the second `agent_message_chunk` contains the full "Goodbye world" (13 chars), not a corrupted byte-offset slice
- Before fix: would emit "d" (offset 11 slice), client renders "Hello worldd"

**"emits the full revised text on a replace delta for a shorter revision"**
- Sends append delta "Hello world!" (12 chars), then replace delta "Hi" (2 chars)
- Asserts the second chunk emits "Hi"
- Before fix: `fullText.length (2) <= sentSoFar (12)` → return early, client stuck on stale text

## Merge Risk

Low — 7 lines added in production code (one `replace` flag extraction, two `replace ? 0 : ...` tracking resets), 167 lines in regression tests. No changes to session handling, prompt lifecycle, or Gateway protocol. The `replace` flag was already defined in the protocol schema and already produced by the Gateway.

- [x] Backwards compatible — normal append deltas are unchanged (replace is undefined/false)
- [x] Existing tests pass — 828/828
- [x] Focused fix — single file, three logical changes

target.title: fix(telegram): strip Markdown formatting in conversation-context dedup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

closes #102257 
Telegram conversation-context dedup fails when the session transcript uses Markdown but the Telegram Bot API cache stores stripped plain text. `resolvePromptContextTextDedupeKey` compares Markdown-rendered text against HTML-stripped Telegram `Message.text`, producing mismatched dedup keys and injecting duplicate assistant rows into the prompt context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dedup key uses `stripMarkdown(stripInlineDirectiveTagsForDelivery(...)).trim()` so both the session transcript and Telegram cache text normalize to the same visible string. Without this fix, a Markdown-formatted message like `**bold**` produces key `bold` from the session but the cache stores literal `**bold**` — never matching → duplicate rows in every follow-up turn.

Additionally, the original fence regex `/```[^\n]*\n?([\s\S]*?)```/g` incorrectly matched inline triple-backtick sequences like ```literal``` in running text. The fix uses `(?<=^|\n)` lookbehind to require fences at line start and a mandatory trailing `\n` before the closing marker.

## User Impact

Without this fix: every conversation turn that includes Markdown-formatted assistant output injects duplicate rows into the prompt, progressively wasting context window and degrading response quality over long conversations.

Without the fence regex fix: `stripMarkdown` would incorrectly strip inline triple-backtick sequences in non-fence contexts (e.g., documentation mentioning ```code```).

## Evidence

**Test Scenario:** Multi-turn conversation with Markdown-formatted assistant responses

function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}
```

This function takes two numbers and returns their sum.
```

**Telegram Cache (Bot API strips HTML tags):**

function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

This function takes two numbers and returns their sum.
```

**Before Fix — Dedup Key Comparison:**

Session:

target.title: fix(sessions): reject malformed history offsets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users requesting `sessions_history` pagination could pass malformed string offsets such as `"1abc"` and have them accepted as offset `1` instead of being rejected before `chat.history` dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the public `sessions_history` tool and the embedded `chat.history` gateway stub now reuse the existing strict non-negative integer parameter reader for `offset`, matching the schema contract and the strict `limit` parsing already used in the same paths. This keeps the fix local to the session history owner boundary and avoids changing pagination behavior for valid numeric offsets.

## User Impact

Malformed offset values are rejected consistently, so session-history pagination cannot silently run from a different page than the caller requested.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: malformed string offsets are rejected in both the public `sessions_history` tool path and the embedded `chat.history` gateway stub path, before malformed pagination can dispatch or read history.
- Current-head real behavior proof at `ea64b57a1a00168496b178f2a97b8932dc22f33a`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` invoked `createSessionsHistoryTool().execute(...)` and `createEmbeddedCallGateway()({ method: "chat.history", ... })` with `offset: "1abc"`.

target.title: fix(doctor): move "target already exists" migration messages from warnings to notices
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103545 — Gateway startup fails when SQLite migration target already exists.

When the shared SQLite state store already contains data from previous migrations (e.g., Memory Core session ingestion, Matrix state, Workboard entries), the gateway startup preflight treats informational "Skipped ... because SQLite already has ..." messages as fatal errors. This blocks startup for users with pre-migrated state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Existing PR #103550 filters warnings by string matching (`includes("because SQLite rows already exist")`), which has three problems:

1. **Incomplete coverage**: The filter only matches Memory Core's 1 warning. Matrix has 5 identical-sentinel warnings ("because SQLite already has ..."), Workboard has 2 ("because the SQLite target already exists"), and ACPX has 1 — all of which cause the same startup blockage but are missed by the string filter.

2. **Fragile string matching**: If any warning message text changes, the filter silently breaks and the original bug re-emerges.

3. **Logic side-effect**: After filtering, when all warnings are informational, the code falls through to `runStartupUpgradeConvergence` — which the original code would skip when warnings exist. This is an unintentional behavior change.

**This PR takes the source-level fix**: Move informational "target already exists" messages from `warnings` to `notices` in the migration functions. The `notices` field already exists in the `PluginDoctorStateMigration` return type and is displayed by `noteStateMigrationResult` as "Doctor notices" — without participating in the startup blocker check. No consumer-side filtering needed.

## Changes

| Extension | Messages moved | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| memory-core | 1 ("because SQLite rows already exist") | `doctor-contract-api.ts` |
| Matrix | 5 ("because SQLite already has ...") | `doctor-contract-api.ts` |
| Workboard | 2 ("because the SQLite target already exists") | `doctor-contract-api.ts` |
| ACPX | 0 (intentionally kept in warnings — "already differs" is a data conflict, not a skip) | — |

Tests updated in `extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` and `extensions/workboard/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` to assert `notices` instead of `warnings` for the moved messages.

## User Impact

Users with legacy workspace state that has already been migrated to SQLite can now start the gateway successfully. The informational notices still appear in the "Doctor notices" output, so operators can see that migrations were skipped — they just no longer block startup.

## Evidence

- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 5/5 passed
- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 6/6 passed
- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 28/28 passed
- [x] No changes to `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` needed — `noteStartupStateMigrationResult` already passes the full result to `noteStateMigrationResult` which displays notices; only `startupMigrationWarnings` (which blocks startup) comes from `result.warnings`, and those no longer contain the informational messages.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  8 passed | 48 skipped (56)
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`); live gateway RPC over WebSocket transport

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed)
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated)
- What you did NOT verify: Live gateway WebSocket transport; cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

target.title: fix(ui): queue chat input while reconnecting
target.body:
Closes #102700

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI kept its reconnect queue alive, but disabled the composer whenever the Gateway disconnected. Users therefore could not add new text or attachments during intermittent connectivity even though the existing queue and session-scoped persistence could safely hold them.

Storage failure was also implicit. An input could appear queued even when browser quota, privacy mode, attachment serialization, or the 50-item bound prevented the exact reconnect item from being stored.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Separate compose availability from live Gateway availability.
- Allow ordinary text and attachment sends to enter the existing per-gateway/session/agent reconnect queue while disconnected.
- Keep slash commands, voice, compaction, goal edits, retry, and steer controls connection-gated.
- Read back the exact queued item before clearing offline input. If storage fails, restore the full composer payload when safe; otherwise keep the item visibly failed without overwriting newer draft work.
- Preserve one idempotency key across reconnect and consume reply context once the queued turn owns it.
- Add deterministic mocked-Gateway online/offline control and browser evidence output.

This reuses the existing bounded queue and current-tab session storage. It does not add cold offline app launch, cross-tab/background sync, or a new storage subsystem.

## User Impact

During an intermittent Gateway outage, an already-loaded Control UI remains writable. Ordinary text and attachments show as **Waiting for reconnect**, survive a same-tab refresh when storage succeeds, and send once after the socket reconnects. If browser storage cannot safely retain the input, the UI does not claim success or silently discard the only copy.

Mobile audit, unchanged by this PR:

- iOS already has a SQLite-backed submitted-message outbox with route scoping, reconnect replay, idempotency, and retry/delete UI. Unsubmitted composer text remains memory-only, and kill/relaunch UI E2E coverage is still missing.
- Android has a Room-backed offline text outbox and reconnect replay, but healthy online sends bypass that durable journal; drafts and offline attachments remain memory-only, and the destructive migration path can erase the queue. Follow-up should journal every text send before network dispatch and replace destructive migration.

## Evidence

- `corepack pnpm test ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts`: 117 passed after the final recovery hardening.
- Focused composer/view/send/persistence/helper suite: 264 passed on the rebased feature.
- `OPENCLAW_BEHAVIOR_PROOF=1 corepack pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts`: 37 passed after the final commit.
- Source-blind behavior proof: composer/send enabled offline; prompt and waiting state stored; 0 offline requests; exactly 1 request after reconnect; idempotency key present; queue cleared after delivery.
- Path-scoped `check:changed`: core and test typechecks, sharded lint, docs/policy/dependency/storage/import guards passed.
- Final targeted core/test `tsgo`, `oxlint`, formatting, and `corepack pnpm build`: passed.
- Autoreview: clean after fixing storage-quota, stale slash-menu, retry-only, and concurrent-draft recovery findings.
- Testbox: `tbx_01kx38dav7vwrv14xea5hgx848`.
- Visual scenario: offline queued state and delivered-after-reconnect state captured from a real Chromium run; artifact links follow on this PR.

## AI Assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, regression tests, mobile/web source audits, source-aware review, and source-blind behavior validation. No transcript is attached.

target.title: fix(skills): reject skill downloads exceeding 100 MB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`downloadFile()` streams response body to disk via `pipeline()` without a byte
limit. A hostile server can send unbounded data, exhausting disk space.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `SKILL_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (100 MiB) enforced via a Transform stream
counter inside the pipeline. The stream is aborted as soon as the byte limit
is exceeded — before excess bytes reach disk. The existing `finally` block
cleans up the temp file and releases the guarded response.

## User Impact

**Before:** no limit — disk exhaustion possible
**After:** 100 MiB enforced in-stream, excess bytes never reach disk, staging
tmp file is removed, and guarded response is released.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/install-download-maxbytes` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 — linux

### Real behavior proof

Two regression tests drive the real production `installDownloadSpec` entry point
(the exact function called by the skill installer). The HTTP layer is mocked
but the full production download pipeline — Transform counter, file write,
staging cleanup, and response release — executes exactly as it does in production.

**Test 1 — oversized download aborted mid-stream (> 100 MiB):**
- A streaming body emits 64 KiB chunks until the counter exceeds 100 MiB
- The Transform counter calls `file.destroy(err)` and `callback(err)`
- `pipeline()` stops forwarding chunks, the stream is destroyed
- Staging `.tmp` file is cleaned up by the `finally` block
- Guarded `release()` is called

**Test 2 — small download completes normally (4 KiB):**
- A 4 KiB body passes through the counter without hitting the limit
- The download completes without any size-limit error
- Guarded `release()` is called

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/lifecycle/install-download.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ installDownloadSpec extraction safety > rejects targetDir escapes outside the per-skill tools root
 ✓ installDownloadSpec extraction safety > allows relative targetDir inside the per-skill tools root
 ✓ installDownloadSpec extraction safety > cancels failed download response bodies before returning the error
 ✓ installDownloadSpec extraction safety > fails closed when the lexical tools root is rebound before the final copy
 ✓ installDownloadSpec download byte limit (#103236) > aborts an oversized download mid-stream and cleans up staging
 ✓ installDownloadSpec download byte limit (#103236) > allows a small download to complete normally
 ✓ installDownloadSpec extraction safety (tar.bz2) > handles tar.bz2 extraction safety edge-cases
 ✓ installDownloadSpec extraction safety (tar.bz2) > rejects tar.bz2 archives that change after preflight
 ✓ installDownloadSpec extraction safety (tar.bz2) > rejects tar.bz2 entries that traverse pre-existing targetDir symlinks

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Diff summary

```
src/skills/lifecycle/install-download.ts       | 24 + (Transform counter + SKILL_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES)
src/skills/lifecycle/install-download.test.ts  | 78 + (2 regression tests for oversized + small downloads)
```

What was not tested: real HTTP server integration (SSRF policy blocks localhost in
proof scripts). The counter logic, abort, cleanup, and release paths are identical
whether the body comes from a real server or a mock — they both go through the same
`pipeline(readable, counter, file)` call.

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
