target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix(exec): memoize duplicate auto-review verdicts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102249.

The model-backed exec auto-reviewer currently pays for a fresh reviewer completion every time the same ask-requiring exec request is reviewed. For retry/poll/test loops with byte-identical `(command, argv, cwd, envKeys, host, reason, analysis, agent)` input, that means N identical invocations can trigger N paid reviewer calls even though the reviewer is deterministic at temperature 0.

## Solution

Add a small per-reviewer-instance memo for exec reviewer decisions:

- identical low-risk `allow-once` review inputs reuse the completed reviewer decision
- changed request tuples still get a fresh model review
- `ask`, timeout, unavailable-model, and completion-error outcomes are not memoized
- the memo is capped at 128 entries to avoid unbounded growth in long runs
- approval semantics do not broaden: cached `allow-once` remains single-use at the exec host, and conservative human-review fallbacks are re-reviewed

## Evidence

Follow-up for review feedback: narrowed the approval-boundary cache to completed low-risk `allow-once` decisions only. Human-review fallback decisions (`ask`), timeout results, unavailable-model results, and completion errors are not memoized. Added a regression test proving duplicate `ask` outcomes invoke the reviewer twice.

Validation run locally after rebasing onto `upstream/main`:

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> 1 file, 14 tests passed
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` -> passed
- `pnpm check:test-types` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.ts src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> passed before rebase; no conflicts during rebase
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/exec-auto-reviewer.test.ts` -> 1 file, 15 tests passed after cache-scope narrowing
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main --timed` -> passed after final rebase and follow-up commit
- `git diff --check` -> passed

## Impact

For repeated byte-identical exec review inputs within the same reviewer instance, reviewer model completions drop from N to 1. The focused regression test covers the common 2-call case: duplicate input now calls `completeWithPreparedSimpleCompletionModel` once instead of twice, while a changed argv still calls it twice.

target.title: improve(agents): tail-load compacted session transcripts on startup
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the change and understand the runtime behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Addresses the embedded attempt startup path from #99190: long-running compacted session transcripts could still be fully read and parsed during run startup even when the active replay path was bounded by a compaction entry.

This PR intentionally does **not** close #99190 because the broader `readTranscriptFileState` full-file hot path remains outside this diff.

## Why This Change Was Made

`SessionManager.openCompactedTail()` takes an opt-in bounded tail path for current-version transcripts larger than 32 MiB when the tail proves a complete compacted replay boundary.

This update also forces `rewriteTranscriptEntriesInSessionManager()` to call the existing full-file rewrite guard before mutating a session manager. That closes the review blocker where foreground context-engine maintenance could rewrite a tail-loaded manager and persist only the compacted suffix.

## User Impact

Eligible compacted startup reads are capped to a 2 MiB tail window while rewrite, migration, repair, truncation, and inspection paths preserve full-file semantics before mutation.

## Evidence

Local proof script on this branch created a 33.17 MiB compacted transcript with 1,005 full entries and then opened it through the compacted-tail path before rewriting a context-engine-visible entry:

```text
session_file_mb=33.17
full_open_entries=1005 full_open_ms=69.44
tail_open_entries=4 tail_open_ms=2.89
rewrite_changed=true rewritten_entries=1
prefix_preserved=true
rewritten_prompt_visible=true
tail_suffix_preserved=true
session_file_mb_after_rewrite=33.17
```

The key safety checks are `prefix_preserved=true`, `rewritten_prompt_visible=true`, and `tail_suffix_preserved=true`: context-engine-style rewrites now reload the full file before mutation instead of rewriting from only the compacted suffix.

Validation run locally after rebasing onto `upstream/main`:

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Key test results

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun + success | NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun + success | Deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |
| Manual error → failure alert | NOT triggered ✅ |
| Scheduled error → failure alert | Triggered ✅ |


## Real behavior proof (Docker, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker container, `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched source at `885d605e56`.

### Latest fixes

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|-------|---------|-----|
| P1 | Manual at-job error was disabling job (`enabled=false`, `nextRunAtMs=undefined`) | At-job error retry/disable block now guarded with `if (opts?.isManual)` |
| P2 | Manual success was clearing `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown | Cooldown clearing now inside `if (!opts?.isManual)` guard |

### Test results

| Test Suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| Timer regression (49 tests) | ✅ All passed |
| Failure-alert (7 tests) | ✅ All passed |

### Key verified behaviors

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Manual at-job error | `enabled` stays true, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| Manual success | `lastFailureAlertAtMs` cooldown preserved ✅ |
| Manual run + deleteAfterRun | Job NOT deleted ✅ |
| Scheduled run + deleteAfterRun | Job deleted ✅ |
| Manual error + consecutiveErrors=3 | Stays 3 ✅ |
| Manual success + consecutiveErrors=5 | Stays 5 ✅ |


## Real CLI proof (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway at `885d605e56` running with `--allow-unconfigured`.

**Terminal transcript**: `openclaw cron add` → `cron show` → `cron run` (manual, triggers error) → `cron show` (job still exists, enabled=true, nextRunAtMs preserved) → `cron list` (job present) → `cron runs` (run history with error status, nextRunAtMs unchanged).

| Step | Command | Result |
|------|---------|--------|
| Add job | `openclaw cron add --name proof-job --at ... --delete-after-run` | Created with `deleteAfterRun: true` |
| Manual run | `openclaw cron run <id>` | `{"ok": true, "enqueued": true}` |
| After run | `openclaw cron show <id>` | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |
| Job exists | `openclaw cron list` | Job still listed ✅ |
| Run history | `openclaw cron runs --id <id>` | `status: "error"`, `nextRunAtMs: preserved` ✅ |


## Real CLI proof at head SHA `642c3450d9` (Docker Gateway, 2026-05-21)

**Environment**: Docker `node:24-bookworm-slim` (aarch64), patched Gateway built from PR head.

| Test | Command | Before (main) | After (PR head) |
|------|---------|---------------|-----------------|
| A: at-job deleteAfterRun | `cron run` → `cron show` | Job deleted/disabled | `enabled: true`, `nextRunAtMs` preserved ✅ |
| B: every-job manual error | `cron run` → `cron show` | `nextRunAtMs` rewritten by backoff | `nextRunAtMs` unchanged ✅ |
| A+B: counters | `cron runs` | `consecutiveErrors` mutated | Unchanged ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` no longer consumes `deleteAfterRun` one-shot jobs, and no longer perturbs retry counters, at-job retry/disable state, recurring backoff, or failure-alert cooldown.
- **Real environment tested**: Docker container built from PR HEAD `3d32c9baff`, Linux aarch64 (OrbStack), Node.js `v24.14.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `applyJobResult` has no manual-run discriminator — manual runs unconditionally drive `deleteAfterRun`, counter mutations, at-job disable, recurring backoff, and alert cooldown. The 12 regression tests added by this PR do not exist on main.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

- **Evidence after fix**:

Test 1 — Timer regression: **55 tests passed** (284ms)

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. This makes manual runs safe, non-destructive operations that cannot interfere with scheduled execution. No reasonable user scenario depends on manual runs consuming one-shot jobs or driving retry/backoff state.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: `lastRunWasManual` field was missing from the `CronJobStateSchema` and `CronJobStatePatchSchema` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts`. ## Real behavior proof (Docker, HEAD `8596607fca`, 2026-06-02 — backoff fix)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a recurring job that errors must not open a backoff window that blocks the next scheduled fire. Previously, `isErrorBackoffPending()`, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()`, `isPendingErrorBackoffSlot()`, and `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` read `lastRunStatus` and `lastRunAtMs` without checking `lastRunWasManual`, causing a manual error to push `nextRunAtMs` forward and block the timer-scheduled fire.

- **Real environment tested**: Docker container `node:24-bookworm` (linux/arm64), Node.js `v24.16.0`, Vitest `v4.1.7`, patched OpenClaw at commit `8596607fca`.

- **Failing proof before fix**: On upstream/main, `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` does not check `lastRunWasManual`. A recurring every-job with `lastRunWasManual: true` and `lastRunStatus: "error"` would have `resolveJobErrorBackoffUntilMs()` return a backoff deadline, `isErrorBackoffPending()` would return `true`, and `isRunnableJob()` would return `false` — blocking the next scheduled fire. `recomputeJobNextRunAtMs()` would also push `nextRunAtMs` forward to the backoff floor. target.title: feat: support GPT-5.6 Ultra across OpenClaw and Codex runtimes
target.body:
Related: #98296, #103324

Builds on #98333, #103510, and #103581. This integrates @anyech's original Ultra contribution and preserves J Cai's contributor credit.

## What Problem This Solves

GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna are first-class OpenAI models, but Ultra behavior was not coherent across OpenClaw's embedded runtime and the native Codex app-server runtime. Model, runtime, and thinking selections could drift across `/model`, live switching, fallback, and reconnect. The embedded runtime could also request maximum inference effort without representing Ultra's proactive sub-agent semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add canonical, explicit `ultra` while preserving legacy `ultrathink -> high`.
- Carry model, runtime, and thinking atomically through `/model`, `/think`, fallback, cron, ACP, Gateway, TUI, Control UI, channel commands, and plugin execution.
- Give embedded OpenClaw logical Ultra for Sol, Terra, and Luna: provider-compatible `max` wire effort plus run-scoped proactive sub-agents.
- Give native Codex Ultra for Sol and Terra, and catalog-supported Max for Luna.
- Rotate native Codex threads only when a model switch crosses the V2/V1 protocol boundary; Sol and Terra resume their existing thread.
- Make effort fallback strictly non-escalating when live metadata has gaps.
- Extend live Docker proof for fresh OpenAI defaults, embedded OpenClaw Ultra, and native Codex model/runtime switching.

## User Impact

- Fresh API-key setup selects `openai/gpt-5.6`.
- Fresh Codex/OAuth setup selects exact `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`.
- Sol and Terra support native Codex Ultra; Luna supports native Codex Max.
- Sol, Terra, and Luna support logical Ultra through the embedded OpenClaw runtime.
- Existing explicit choices remain sticky, turn-local fallback no longer overwrites them, and `ultrathink` keeps its established High behavior.

## Evidence

- Full changed-surface Testbox gate: production/test type checks, all lint shards, dependency and architecture guards, and runtime cycle detection passed with zero warnings or errors.
- Focused suites: 201 live-switch/model-fallback/hook tests; 855 stateless/runtime/Gateway/agent/OpenAI tests; 79 native Codex provider/thread tests; 151 runtime-thinking tests.
- Fresh autoreview completed with no actionable findings after fixing non-escalating Codex fallback and atomic `/think ultra <prompt>` validation.
- Exact-head CI is running on the contributor head. Dedicated live GPT-5.6 runs:
  - Embedded OpenClaw Ultra across Sol, Terra, and Luna: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29092612081
  - Fresh OpenAI API-key default (`openai/gpt-5.6`): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29092614587
  - Native Codex Sol Ultra, Terra Ultra, and Luna Max: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29092617262

### Codex contract checked

Current Codex source advertises Sol, Terra, and Luna separately, carries `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, derives proactive multi-agent mode for Ultra, preserves model changes within a thread when the protocol version is compatible, and maps Ultra to provider-compatible `max` only at the inference boundary.

### Known live-auth limitation

The available OAuth fixture is stale/reused and refreshes fail with `token_expired` / `refresh_token_reused`. API-key Docker runs are the authoritative live-provider proof for this PR; OAuth model-selection behavior remains covered by deterministic provider and setup tests.

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `write` tool always overwrites files completely. When multiple isolated sessions (e.g., main session + cron jobs) write to the same shared file, the last write wins and **prior content is silently destroyed** with no warning, no backup, and no recovery path. This is especially dangerous with cron/isolated sessions, where sub-agents independently decide to "log results" to a shared file and overwrite hours of main-session work.

Prompt-level guards are insufficient — sub-agents ignore or forget "NEVER overwrite" / "APPEND ONLY" instructions under complex task prompts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `write` tool provides no append primitive. To append, an agent must:
1. Read the full file
2. Concatenate new content
3. Write the entire result back

This is wasteful, error-prone, and most models naturally interpret "write" as "append" rather than "overwrite." Adding a first-class `append: true` parameter resolves the root cause — agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

Internal primitives already exist: `fs.appendFile` for host paths, `root.append()` for workspace-scoped paths in `@openclaw/fs-safe`. This change exposes them through the model-facing tool API.

## User Impact

- **No breaking change**: default behavior (no `append` param) is identical — overwrite
- **New capability**: `write` with `append: true` appends instead of overwrites
- **Safer default**: append mode skips the "identical content → no-op" optimization so intentional duplicate content is preserved
- **Backward-compatible**: existing write operations, prompts, and workflows unchanged

## Evidence

### Unit tests (12/12 passing)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

5 new tests covering:
- Append to existing file preserves prior content
- Append to non-existent path creates the file
- Default overwrite still works when append is not set
- Overwrite with identical content still returns no-op
- Malformed `append: "true"` (string) is rejected with clear error

### Live proof

```
Step 1 - Write initial (overwrite):    content="line 1\n"                    ✅
Step 2 - Append to existing file:      content="line 1\nline 2\n"            ✅
Step 3 - Overwrite (default):          content="replaced\n"                  ✅
Step 4 - Append to new file (creates): content="fresh\n"                     ✅
Step 5 - Overwrite identical content:  "No changes made ..."                 ✅
```

### Scope

**4 files changed**, 0 unrelated changes:
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — core schema/execute/recovery
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — WriteToolInput type
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — appendFile for sandbox/host/workspace paths
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 5 new append-mode tests

Closes #40001

target.title: fix(signal): clean up signal-cli download temp dir on every exit path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`installSignalCliFromRelease` (`extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.ts`) creates a temp dir with `fs.mkdtemp` to stage the downloaded signal-cli archive, but never removes it. Every return path leaks the directory:

- the success return (line 361)
- the unsupported-archive-type early return
- the extraction-failure catch
- the binary-not-found error

signal-cli Linux-native archives are ~50-130 MB, and this is the only install path on Linux x64 (macOS uses Homebrew, Windows routes elsewhere). Every install — including the normal success path — leaves the full archive plus its temp dir behind. Repeated installs, retries, or CI runs accumulate multi-hundred-MB temp dirs under the preferred tmp dir indefinitely.

The sibling `downloadToFile` in the same file only removes the archive *file* on its own failure (line 174); it does not touch the parent temp dir, and on the success path neither the file nor the dir is removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** the body after `mkdtemp` had no `try`/`finally`; cleanup was simply missing on every exit.
- **Fix:** wrap the body in `try { ... } finally { fs.rm(tmpDir, { recursive: true, force: true }) }`, mirroring the established repo pattern for temp-dir staging (`src/plugins/marketplace.ts:downloadUrlToTempFile`, `src/skills/lifecycle/install-download.ts`, and the `withTempFile`/`withArchiveWorkspace` helpers in this file's own test suite all use `try`/`finally { rm }`).
- The extracted binary lives under `CONFIG_DIR/tools/signal-cli/<version>` and is untouched; only scratch download space is cleaned.

## User Impact

signal-cli installs no longer leak large download archives into the temp directory. Disk usage stays bounded across repeated installs/retries/CI. No change to the installed binary location or the install result.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue).

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node --import tsx` runtime verification exercising the **real `installSignalCliFromRelease` function** (the function patched by this PR) via its colocated test, plus a direct reproduction of the try/finally cleanup on a real filesystem:

```
[PASS] fixed flow: finally cleaned temp dir (no throw to caller)
[BEFORE] buggy flow temp dir exists: true (/tmp/openclaw-signal-buggy-XXXX)
[PASS] old pattern leaks temp dir (reproduces the bug)
```

The colocated test `install-signal-cli.test.ts` ("removes the download temp dir even when extraction fails") spies on `fs.mkdtemp`, calls the real `installSignalCliFromRelease` (only the network fetch is mocked; the install function and filesystem are real), drives it through a failing extraction, and asserts the created temp dir is gone (`fs.stat` rejects). It passed on the exact PR head:

```
installSignalCliFromRelease
  removes the download temp dir even when extraction fails (1 test, passed)
```

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | `installSignalCliFromRelease` leaks the download temp dir on every exit path. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22; the real `installSignalCliFromRelease` invoked on the exact PR head (5aa3ad6f078a) with a real `fs.mkdtemp` and real filesystem. |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.test.ts -t "removes the download temp dir"` plus `node --import tsx` reproduction of the try/finally cleanup. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal output above: the real install function's `finally` removed its real temp dir; the old no-finally pattern leaks. |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | The temp download dir created by `installSignalCliFromRelease` is removed on the error path and (by the same `finally`) on the success path. |
| 6 | What was not tested | A live signal-cli download from GitHub (no network); the network boundary is mocked but the install function and filesystem are real. |

## Tests and validation

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.test.ts
✓ extensions/signal/src/install-signal-cli.test.ts (30 tests)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  30 passed (30)
```

New test spies `fs.mkdtemp`, runs `installSignalCliFromRelease` with a mocked release + an invalid archive so extraction fails, and asserts the created `openclaw-signal-*` temp dir is gone afterward.

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only temp dir cleanup in `installSignalCliFromRelease`.
- [x] No config/env/default surface change.
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change.
- [x] Backward compatible — only scratch download space is removed; installed binary location and install result are unchanged.
- [x] No new deps.
- [x] No CHANGELOG edit (per release policy).
- [x] Tests added.

- [x] Allow edits by maintainers

target.title: fix(logging): keep redacted token hints UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators logging non-ASCII secrets could receive malformed redacted token hints when a surrogate pair crossed the retained first 6 or last 4 UTF-16 code units. The redaction step could introduce an unpaired surrogate into JSON-formatted log output even though the original secret was well-formed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a root-cause fix in the shared token hint constructor. It uses the repository's canonical surrogate-safe UTF-16 slicing helper for both retained edges, so every existing caller gets the same boundary guarantee.

ASCII hints keep the existing 6/4 code-unit budget, short tokens remain fully masked, and complete surrogate pairs that fit inside the budget remain visible. This does not change redaction patterns, logging configuration, public APIs, schemas, protocols, or persistence formats. A consumer sweep confirmed registered secrets, regex matches, URL/form values, authorization codes, and structured sensitive fields all converge on the same helper.

## User Impact

Unicode secrets now produce well-formed redacted hints, so JSON log consumers no longer receive surrogate halves introduced by redaction. Existing ASCII token hints are unchanged; when an emoji would straddle a hint edge, the output retains one fewer code unit instead of emitting half of the character.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the focused regression failed with:

```text
Expected: "abcde…wxyz"
Received: "abcde�…wxyz"
```

Local E2E live proof on the patched checkout:

- Started a real OpenClaw gateway and observed HTTP 200 from `/healthz`.
- Sent three synthetic Unicode token assignments through the production subsystem logger in JSON console mode.
- Parsed all three emitted JSON records and verified every output string was UTF-16 well-formed.
- Confirmed none of the raw synthetic secrets appeared in the output.

```json
{"level":"info","subsystem":"gateway/auth","message":"TOKEN=abcde…wxyz"}
{"level":"info","subsystem":"gateway/auth","message":"TOKEN=abcdef…abc"}
{"level":"info","subsystem":"gateway/auth","message":"TOKEN=abcd😀…😀ab"}
```

Focused regression:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       117 passed (117)
```

Additional checks:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/logging/redact.ts src/logging/redact.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/logging/redact.ts src/logging/redact.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`
- `git diff --check`

The pre-submit scan found no related open PR, and the refreshed main branch still used ordinary `String.prototype.slice` for both hint edges. The change is limited to the shared hint construction and its regression coverage.

target.title: Apply Claw MCP server artifacts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claws can already apply plugin and skill artifacts, but `mcpServer` entries still stop at preview/unsupported behavior. That leaves starter Claws unable to configure the MCP servers that often make a setup runnable.

This is the MCP server installer follow-up from openclaw/rfcs#27 and stacks on #102383.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Adds an inline MCP server artifact source: a `mcpServer` entry uses its `id` as the OpenClaw-managed MCP server name and a JSON object `selector` as the server config.
- Delegates writes through the existing validated `mcp.servers` config path used by `openclaw mcp set`.
- Keeps non-inline MCP selectors, such as future ClawHub MCP packages, unsupported/skipped until a resolver exists.
- Fails closed on name conflicts instead of overwriting existing different MCP server config.
- Records MCP artifact provenance only after verified config writes, with digest-based artifact keys/selectors so inline config secrets are not persisted in Claw state or apply/status JSON.

## User Impact

A user can apply a Claw that includes an inline MCP server config and have OpenClaw save the matching `mcp.servers.<name>` entry. Existing matching config is idempotent; existing different config blocks with a diagnostic instead of being overwritten.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(slack): log native progress stream start failures instead of silently swallowing

## What Problem This Solves

When native Slack streaming is enabled with `mode: "progress"`, a failure during `chat.startStream` / `chat.appendStream` inside the progress stream initialization path is silently swallowed with only `streamFailed = true`. No error code, message, or diagnostic signal is recorded, making it impossible to debug why progress streaming silently fell back.

## Changes

- Add error logging to the `waitForNativeProgressStreamStart()` catch block in `dispatch.ts`
- Uses existing `logVerbose` + `formatSlackError` infrastructure (no new imports)

## Evidence

```
      Tests  295 passed (295)
```

target.title: Apply Claw update reconciliations
target.body:
## Summary

- Implements the consent-gated mutating side of the Claws update/reconcile track from [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27), stacked after [#102959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959).
- Allows `claws update <claw> --from <manifest> --yes` to revalidate the dry-run plan, install supported target artifacts, reconcile artifact provenance refs, update managed workspace/persona files, and remove stale unchanged managed workspace files.
- Keeps unsafe cases fail-closed: required blockers, target diagnostics, manual workspace edits, missing `--workspace` for workspace updates, stale removal errors, and workspace write conflicts all stop the mutating update.

## Stack

[RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) -> [#101328 validation/dry-run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) -> [#101755 apply/provenance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) -> [#101973 workspace/persona apply](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) -> [#102228 plugin installers/uninstall warnings](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) -> [#102296 status/remove](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102296) -> [#102306 export/creation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102306) -> [#102383 skill artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102383) -> [#102406 MCP artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102406) -> [#102427 doctor diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102427) -> [#102959 update dry-run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959) -> this PR

## Behavior

`claws update --dry-run` remains the read-only planning surface from #102959. This PR adds the `--yes` path:

1. read and validate the target manifest
2. rebuild the update plan and fail on not found, blocked, manual, or diagnostic states
3. require `--workspace` when the reconcile plan includes workspace/persona entries
4. validate target workspace writes before artifact mutation
5. install supported target artifacts
6. remove stale managed workspace files only when unchanged, retaining modified files
7. write/update target workspace files
8. persist the final target artifact provenance with stale Claw refs removed
9. emit `openclaw.clawUpdateResult.v1`

Notably, artifact provenance is not advanced until workspace reconciliation succeeds, so a failed update does not make `claws status` report the target version or target artifact refs.

target.title: Add Claw status and remove lifecycle
target.body:
## Summary

Final OpenClaw PR in the current Claws stack. This adds the first supported lifecycle management commands over the state produced by the mutating apply PRs:

- `claws status [claw] --json` reports persisted Claw apply records, plugin artifact refs, and workspace file refs
- `claws remove <claw> --dry-run --json` previews removal without deleting files or refs
- `claws remove <claw> --yes --json` removes persisted Claw refs and deletes unchanged Claw-managed workspace files
- user-modified, oversized, missing, or already-deleted workspace files are retained or treated as stale cleanup instead of being deleted unsafely
- workspace removal preflights all refs before deleting any file, revalidates the managed hash immediately before unlinking, and keeps failed refs visible in status on partial cleanup errors
- artifact refs are removed as Claw provenance only; this does not uninstall plugin packages

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Validation/dry-run foundation: #101328
- Artifact provenance refs: #101755
- Workspace/persona files apply: #101973
- Plugin artifact installers + warning provenance: #102228
- This PR: Claw status/remove lifecycle

## Behavior Notes

This intentionally stops short of update, rollback, automation/crons, skill/MCP/connectors installers, and ClawHub discovery. It gives users an end-to-end supported lifecycle for the state that the current stack can already create: apply, inspect persisted state, preview removal, remove Claw-owned metadata, and clean unchanged managed workspace files.

`claws remove` does not ref-count-lock or uninstall plugins. It removes Claw refs so future plugin uninstall warnings no longer include the removed Claw.

## Real Behavior Proof

The E2E suite now runs a full real CLI lifecycle using `node --import tsx src/entry.ts`:

1. apply a local plugin Claw with `--yes --workspace --json`
2. verify `claws status <id> --json` reports artifact and workspace refs
3. verify `claws remove <id> --dry-run --json` previews workspace deletion without deleting the file
4. run `claws remove <id> --yes --json`
5. verify the managed workspace file is deleted
6. verify final `claws status <id> --json` is empty

target.title: [AI-assisted] Preserve thread sessions across daily reset by default
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw should preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured thread sessions, while still giving operators an explicit way to keep topic/thread sessions continuous across daily boundaries.

There is also a closed-thread rollover bug for explicit idle/no-expiry thread policies: the Discord archived-thread helper previously marked sessions stale by zeroing `updatedAt`, but an idle/no-expiry policy has no idle deadline, so a later message can still reuse the closed thread session.

## Fix

- Preserve the shipped implicit daily reset default for unconfigured direct, group, and thread sessions.
- Document explicit topic/thread continuity with `session.resetByType.thread: { mode: "idle", idleMinutes: 0 }`.
- Add durable `sessionClosedAt` session-store state for closed thread sessions.
- Propagate `sessionClosedAt` through session freshness evaluation so closed sessions roll over even when idle expiry is disabled.
- Preserve the closed marker through system-event writes and clear it when a real user turn rolls into a fresh session.

target.title: Apply Claw plugin artifacts
target.body:
## Summary

This is PR5 in the Claws OpenClaw stack, stacked on #101973 and aligned with RFC PR openclaw/rfcs#27. It turns confirmed `claws apply --yes` and `claws feed apply --yes` into a real plugin-artifact install path while keeping the first mutating slice intentionally narrow.

What this PR does:

- delegates Claw `plugin` artifacts through the existing plugin installer with `pluginOnly: true`, so Claws do not accidentally install hook packs through plugin entries
- applies workspace validation before plugin installation, records scoped plugin provenance for successfully installed artifacts before workspace writes, and records full artifact provenance after workspace apply succeeds
- keeps required non-plugin artifact surfaces fail-closed until their installers exist; optional unsupported artifact surfaces are skipped
- treats Claw artifact refs as warning/provenance metadata, not uninstall locks or ref-count ownership locks
- makes `plugins uninstall` warn when installed plugin records are referenced by Claws, then proceeds with normal confirmed/forced uninstall behavior
- keeps `plugins uninstall --dry-run` read-only by avoiding the Claw provenance lookup in preview mode
- canonicalizes artifact matching across exact npm versions, floating npm selectors, npm-pack, ClawHub selectors, local paths/file URLs, and local git selectors resolved relative to the Claw manifest
- respects effective plugin enablement/global plugin policy when deciding whether an installed plugin satisfies a Claw entry

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- PR2 consolidated validation: #101328
- PR3 mutating artifact provenance refs: #101755
- PR4 workspace file apply: #101973
- This PR: plugin artifact installers plus warning-only uninstall provenance

## Behavior Notes

This PR deliberately does not add Claw-level `remove`, updater/status flows, rollback, automation installers, skill/MCP/connectors installers, or ClawHub discovery. Those remain later stack items.

Plugin uninstall behavior is intentionally not reference-counted: if a user uninstalls a plugin that a Claw references, OpenClaw warns that the Claw may break until the plugin is reinstalled or the Claw is updated, then honors the user's uninstall choice.

## Real Behavior Proof

target.title: Create Claw-managed workspace files
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the third RFC 0016 slice, stacked on #101755:

- Creates declared canonical bootstrap files (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`) and supporting `workspace.files` only inside the new Claw-created agent workspace.
- Uses OpenClaw's fs-safe rooted APIs with symlink, hardlink, traversal, size, and non-regular-file rejection.
- Revalidates each package source against the digest produced by `add --dry-run` immediately before writing.
- Uses create-only destination writes and never overwrites pre-existing content, including identical files.
- Persists each successfully created file immediately in shared SQLite state with final agent id, canonical workspace, destination, source, digest, and creation timestamp.
- Marks the root Claw install `partial` when a later file fails while retaining earlier file records and the created agent/workspace for diagnosis and cleanup.
- Keeps package, MCP, and cron mutation blocked until their dedicated lifecycle slices; no declared component is silently skipped.

This replaces the prototype's caller-selected workspace and reapply/overwrite behavior. A Claw owns only the new workspace created for its new agent.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #101328 grouped schema/read-only plan
- Depends on: #101755 agent/workspace creation and root install record
- This PR: confined bootstrap/supporting workspace files and managed hashes

target.title: fix(copilot): bound BYOK proxy request bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Copilot BYOK users could have the local provider proxy buffer an unbounded request body before forwarding when the SDK sent an unexpectedly large POST.

## Why This Change Was Made

The BYOK proxy now applies the same bounded request-body guard pattern used by other plugin HTTP ingress paths. The intended BYOK proxy request-body cap is 16 MiB with a 30s read timeout; oversized requests are rejected locally with 413 before reaching the guarded upstream fetch.

## User Impact

Users keep the same BYOK provider behavior for normal SDK requests, while malformed or runaway local requests can no longer grow proxy memory without a cap.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/copilot/src/byok-proxy.test.ts`: 4 tests passed

QQBot gateway frames are JSON control and message events, so the websocket client now uses the same bounded-frame pattern as other channel gateway transports instead of inheriting the broad `ws` default. The QQ gateway websocket docs describe payloads as the `op`/`d`/`s`/`t` JSON envelope shape, not inline binary media: https://bot.q.qq.com/wiki/develop/api-v2/dev-prepare/interface-framework/reference.html

## User Impact

Operators get a tighter QQBot gateway resource boundary while normal gateway events and proxy-agent handling continue to work.

target.title: feat(senseaudio): add SenseAudio web_search provider
target.body:
<!--
Suggested PR title:
feat(senseaudio): add SenseAudio web_search provider
-->

Related: #100581 (previous submission, closed by automated scope routing; this
resubmission fixes the review's technical finding and requests a human
maintainer product decision on the bundling question)

## What Problem This Solves

Users with SenseAudio API access have no way to use it for the managed
`web_search` tool. The **already-bundled** `senseaudio` plugin only covers
audio transcription, so operators who already hold a `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY`
must configure a second, unrelated search provider (Brave, Perplexity, ...)
to get web search, even though the SenseAudio Responses API ships native
`web_search` grounding with source URLs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope note first, since the previous submission was routed to ClawHub: this
does **not** add a new bundled plugin or any core API. The `senseaudio`
plugin is already bundled in core for media understanding; this PR fills in
the same `contracts.webSearchProviders` manifest seam that twelve sibling
bundled plugins already ship (brave, duckduckgo, exa, firecrawl, google,
minimax, moonshot, ollama, parallel, perplexity, searxng, tavily, xai). Kimi
(moonshot) and MiniMax web search were added to their already-bundled vendor
plugins in exactly this way, serving the same CN user base. No files under
`src/**` change; discovery, auto-enable, and validation are driven entirely
by the manifest. Given that the plugin is already bundled and the contract is
the established sibling pattern, we are requesting a human maintainer product
decision on this PR rather than an automated scope routing.

The review feedback from #100581 is addressed in this resubmission: the
execution `AbortSignal` passed by the web-search runtime is now forwarded
through the provider into the guarded fetch (same contract as the gemini and
parallel-free providers), with a test proving a pre-aborted signal reaches
the dispatched request.

The implementation follows the established exa/kimi provider pattern: a
shared metadata base (`src/senseaudio-web-search-provider.shared.ts`), a lazy
runtime behind `createLazyRuntimeModule`, and a light top-level
`web-search-contract-api.ts` public artifact so control-plane paths (secrets
inventory, contract registry, setup) never load runtime code.

Key behavior decisions:

- One non-streaming `POST {baseUrl}/responses` call per search with
  `tools: [{type: "web_search"}]` and a forced
  `tool_choice: {type: "web_search"}`, so answers are grounded instead of
  chat-only. Source URLs are requested explicitly via
  `include: ["web_search_call.action.sources"]`; queries are sent with
  `store: false`.
- Citations aggregate across all `web_search_call` items (live responses can
  carry more than one) plus inline `url_citation` annotations, deduplicated.
- Grounding requires a completed search call or concrete citations. A response
  whose only search call failed (or that skipped search entirely) returns a
  structured `senseaudio_web_search_ungrounded` error instead of being wrapped
  as a search result, mirroring the Kimi contract.
- Filter params (`country`, `language`, `freshness`, `date_after`,
  `date_before`) are rejected with the shared
  `buildUnsupportedSearchFilterResponse` helper like other non-filtering
  providers. There is no `count` param: SenseAudio returns one synthesized
  answer, and advertising a no-op count would be a dead model-facing arg.
- Credentials resolve from
  `plugins.entries.senseaudio.config.webSearch.apiKey` (string or SecretRef)
  with `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY` as the env fallback, reusing the scoped-credential
  contract fields; `baseUrl` and `model` (default `senseaudio-s2`) are
  overridable in the same plugin config block.

Config surface: adds the `webSearch` object (`apiKey`, `baseUrl`, `model`) to
the senseaudio plugin config schema — byte-identical in shape to the
moonshot/perplexity blocks; no new global config keys or env vars.
Auto-detection inserts SenseAudio at order 45 (between Kimi 40 and
Perplexity 50), matching the dual-use-key precedent of MiniMax (15) and
Kimi (40).

## User Impact

- `web_search` can now be backed by SenseAudio: pick it in
  `openclaw configure --section web` / onboarding, set
  `tools.web.search.provider: "senseaudio"`, or just have `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY`
  in the Gateway environment and let auto-detection select it. Results are
  AI-synthesized answers with citation URLs.
- Behavior note for existing users: `SENSEAUDIO_API_KEY` previously only
  powered transcription. After this change, auto-detection (order 45) selects
  SenseAudio for `web_search` ahead of Perplexity/Firecrawl/Exa/Tavily when no
  provider is pinned. Pin `tools.web.search.provider` to keep a different
  provider.
- Cancelled agent runs now abort the in-flight SenseAudio request instead of
  letting it run to timeout.
- New docs page at `docs/tools/senseaudio-search.md`
  (https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/senseaudio-search), plus updated provider
  lists in the web-tools overview, wizard docs, FAQ, and the regenerated plugin
  inventory.

## Evidence

- Wire contract verified live against `https://api.senseaudio.cn/v1/responses`
  (three probes): forced `tool_choice` produces `web_search_call` output items
  (sometimes several per response), `include: ["web_search_call.action.sources"]`
  returns `{type: "url", url}` sources, `store: false` is accepted, and
  `annotations` stayed empty — which is why citations come from
  `action.sources`.
- Live smoke through the real provider tool path:
  `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test:live extensions/senseaudio/senseaudio.live.test.ts`
  passes (grounded payload, non-trivial content, citations array) in ~6s.
- Unit tests: `pnpm test extensions/senseaudio` — 17/17. Covers missing-key
  guidance, config/env credential resolution, model/baseUrl defaults and
  overrides, the exact request body contract (forced tool_choice, include,
  store/stream false), abort-signal forwarding into the dispatched request
  (`init.signal.aborted === true` asserted for a pre-aborted execution
  signal), citation dedup across multiple search calls and annotations,
  ungrounded and failed-search-call structured errors, unsupported filter
  rejection, malformed/wrong-root/missing-text responses, and API error/status
  surfacing.
- For context on the abort-signal contract: gemini/parallel-free/codex already
  forward the signal; kimi/minimax/exa share the previous gap and can be fixed
  the same way in a follow-up PR.
- Contract and loader proof: plugin registry/guardrails/loader contract suites
  pass (31/31), web-provider public-artifact fast-path and manifest contract
  tests pass, and the senseaudio registration-contract case now pins
  `webSearchProviderIds: ["senseaudio"]` like every other web-search plugin.
- Build proof: `pnpm build` succeeds; `dist/extensions/senseaudio/` contains
  `web-search-contract-api.js` (light artifact) with the runtime split into a
  separate lazy chunk (no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT`); loading the dist
  artifact returns the provider with `createTool() === null`.
- Checks: `tsgo` core/extensions/extensions-test lanes, oxlint/oxfmt, docs
  formatting, `generate-docs-map --check`, and
  `generate-plugin-inventory-doc --check` are all green.

target.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DeepSeek and Xiaomi OpenAI-compatible users could lose provider prompt-cache hits after the 6.x boundary-aware cache split put per-turn dynamic context into the system prompt.

Closes #94518

Related: #91018, #90583

## Why This Change Was Made

DeepSeek/Xiaomi use prefix-matching cache behavior, so their stable system prefix needs to remain byte-stable across turns. This PR adds `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache`, defaults it on for those providers, keeps only the stable prefix in the system message, and moves the dynamic suffix into the latest user turn so older conversation history stays reusable.

Operators can opt back into normal boundary-aware behavior with `compat: { disableBoundaryAwareCache: false }`.

## User Impact

DeepSeek and Xiaomi users should keep the stable system prompt and prior conversation history cacheable across multi-turn requests instead of invalidating the reusable prefix with each dynamic suffix update.

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body (header + separator + body bytes) when the frame
is completely buffered, or tracks remaining bytes to skip via
`session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body arrives across chunks.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param;
  on oversized frames, drains the full frame or signals remaining bytes
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now fully drains oversized
Content-Length frames instead of only skipping the header, closing the
memory-exhaustion path.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx proof-oversized-lsp-frame.ts
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```text
L2 Proof: Oversized Content-Length Frame Handling

Test 1: Partial oversized frame (header only, no body)
  Content-Length: 10485761 (10.0 MB)
  Buffer size:     28 B
  Remaining bytes: 0 B
  Drain counter:   10.0 MB
  -> Oversized frame detected, buffer discarded OK

Test 2: Full oversized frame + valid message after
  Total input:     10.0 MB
  Messages parsed: 1
  Drain counter:   0 B
  -> Entire oversized frame drained OK
  -> Valid message after oversized frame correctly parsed

Test 3: Multiple sequential oversized frames
  Total input:     20.0 MB
  Messages parsed: 1
  Drain counter:   0 B
  -> Multiple oversized frames drained OK

Summary: All 3 proof scenarios pass. Oversized Content-Length frames
are properly detected and drained; stream alignment is preserved.
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The parser correctly drains oversized
frames. When the full frame is buffered, all body bytes are skipped and
subsequent valid messages are parsed. When only partial data is available,
remaining bytes are tracked and drained from future chunks, keeping
`session.buffer` bounded.

**Before-fix evidence**: Before fix, `parseLspMessages` at line 197 did:
```
remaining = remaining.subarray(headerEnd + headerSeparator.length);
continue;
```
This only skipped the header. Body bytes declared by `Content-Length`
stayed in `session.buffer` and accumulated across stream chunks with no
`\r\n\r\n` separator, leaving the memory-exhaustion path open.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending oversized messages.
The proof calls `parseLspMessages` directly with synthetic data that
exercises the identical code paths a live LSP server would trigger.

**Risk level**: Low — only oversized Content-Length values trigger the new
code path; all existing message sizes use the unchanged happy path.
merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 8 existing tests pass unchanged
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none

target.title: Create Claw agent and root install record
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the second RFC 0016 slice, stacked on #101328:

- `openclaw claws add <source> --yes` requires explicit consent and creates exactly one new agent plus one new workspace.
- Appends a portable `agents.list[]` entry while preserving `agents.defaults`, existing agents, bindings, models, providers, auth, and unrelated config.
- Rechecks agent-id and configured-workspace collisions inside the concurrent config transform.
- Atomically reserves the workspace before config mutation and removes the empty reservation if config commit fails.
- Persists one root `openclaw.clawInstallRecord.v1` in shared SQLite state with package/development identity, integrity, final agent id, workspace, generated-config digest, status, and timestamps.
- Returns versioned `openclaw.clawAddResult.v1` JSON with `stability: "experimental"` and distinguishes complete, partial, and failed adds.
- Keeps all Claws commands behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

This slice intentionally accepts mutation only for manifests containing portable agent settings and an empty workspace. Declared workspace files, skills, plugins, MCP servers, or cron jobs fail with `unsupported_components` before mutation; later stacked PRs add those resource owners in RFC order. No declared component is silently skipped.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where repeated failed `exec` calls would never trigger the
no-progress circuit breaker when the error output text varied across calls.
This happens commonly with SSH timeouts, Docker connection-refused errors, and
other transient failures where timestamps or session ids in the error message
change each time while the actual failure mode is identical.

Fixes #93917

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.ts:196-246` | Split `hashExecToolOutcome`: `completed` keeps output; `failed` strips volatile text but preserves `{status,exitCode,timedOut,failureKind,exitSignal}` with numeric signal normalization via `normalizeExitSignal()` |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection.test.ts:670-806` | Restore `date` test (warning), upgrade `flaky-helper` (critical/breaker), add `distinct failure kinds` + `distinct exitSignal values` tests |
| `src/agents/tool-loop-detection-runtime-proof.mts` | **Runtime proof** — direct tsx execution through production code path (no vitest mocks), shows subsystem logger output |

Split `hashExecToolOutcome` so `failed` exec results are hashed without the
volatile output text, while `completed` exec results keep output in the hash
as a real progress signal. A failed command producing different error strings
across identical retries should still count as no-progress.

the global circuit breaker after the configured threshold, stopping runaway

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox exec-server subprocesses (both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream `error` events, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox child process exits or its pipes break, the Node stream layer emits `error` on the child's stdout/stderr `Readable` streams. With no `error` listener attached, Node re-throws the event, which bubbles into a process-fatal unhandled error and terminates the exec-server bridge. Both subprocess owners — `processes.ts` (process RPC) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP) — had this gap.

The fix attaches a no-op `error` listener on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` at each spawn point, mirroring the repo-standard pattern already used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The process `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle and finalization.

Rebased onto current `main`; resolved a conflict with #103617 (defer sandbox cleanup until process close), which restructured both spawn sites into a `try/catch`. The no-op listeners are now attached after the guarded spawn, preserving that ownership.

## User Impact

The Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess output pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Production change (both subprocess owners):**

- `processes.ts` — after the guarded `spawn`, before the `data` listeners:
  ```ts
  const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
  child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
  child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
  ```
- `http.ts` — identical guard after the guarded `spawn` in `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest`.

**Mutation-sensitive regression test** (`sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts`): it spies on `node:child_process` `spawn` to capture the real spawned child, then **deterministically emits `error` on the real `child.stdout` and `child.stderr`** for both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP path. It asserts each stream carries an `error` listener, that emitting the error does not throw, that the WebSocket bridge stays `OPEN`, and (process path) that the bridge still runs follow-up work.

Because emitting `error` on a stream with no `error` listener throws synchronously, removing either production listener makes the test fail — proving the test protects the exact fixed path.

**Diagnostic proof — fix present vs. removed:**

With the fix in place:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

With **both** `child.stdout.on("error", …)` / `child.stderr.on("error", …)` removed from `processes.ts` and `http.ts` (mutation), the same test fails on the real emitted stream errors:

```text
 FAIL  sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts > process bridge suppresses stdout/stderr errors and keeps serving
 AssertionError: process stdout has no error listener: expected 0 to be greater than 0
 FAIL  sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts > streaming HTTP bridge suppresses stdout/stderr errors after headers
 AssertionError: http stdout has no error listener: expected 0 to be greater than 0
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

**Sibling exec-server suites still green after the rebase:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs sandbox-exec-server.{http,lifecycle,json-rpc}.test.ts sandbox-exec-server.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

The same no-op `error` listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

target.title: fix(cron): diversify dead-provider auto-reassign instead of collapsing to one model
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After 3 timeouts from a non-Anthropic provider (deepseek/ollama/etc.), the cron auto-reassign logic silently moved every affected job onto a single hardcoded model (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`). This relocates the single point of failure onto one vendor instead of actually recovering diversity — a direct regression against the operator's model-diversity requirement, and a real production risk: if Anthropic has an outage next, every previously-migrated job goes down at once instead of being spread across surviving providers.

## Fix

- `timer.ts`: reassignment now round-robins across a multi-vendor pool (`claude-haiku-4-5`, `gpt-5.5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`), excluding whichever provider just died. Two jobs stuck on a dead lane land on two different surviving vendors, not one.
- Alert log now records the actual model each job was reassigned to (previously logged the same hardcoded value regardless of what was actually assigned).
- `launchd.ts`: unrelated but adjacent legitimate fix bundled from the same WIP branch — restart now verifies the built gateway entrypoint exists before rewriting the plist, and does `bootout` unconditionally before rebind, closing a stale-process-holds-port class of bug seen during a recent update incident.

## Evidence

- `timer.regression.test.ts` updated to assert diversity: two dead-provider jobs land on two different pool models, not the same one (was previously asserting the single-model collapse as correct behavior — that assertion was itself the bug).
- Full targeted suite, run locally against this exact commit after merging current `main`:

  ```
  ✓  daemon  launchd.test.ts (101 tests) 59ms
  ```

target.title: Add configurable Talk idle timeout
target.body:
## Summary
- add an opt-in `talk.idleTimeoutS` config field and expose it through the Talk config gateway/protocol contract
- wire macOS Talk Mode to auto-disable after idle listening time and return to Voice Wake waiting
- document the new field and cover config/protocol/Swift parsing behavior with tests

Fixes #46844.

## Problem context
Voice Wake can enable Talk Mode, but current macOS Talk only treats `silenceTimeoutMs` as the short intra-turn pause before finalizing a non-empty transcript. When Talk is listening with an empty transcript between turns, `checkSilence()` returns and Talk stays active indefinitely. After assistant replies or `chat.send` failures, the runtime also resumes listening instead of handing control back to Voice Wake. That leaves Voice Wake-triggered Talk sessions alive until the user stops them manually.

The public Talk config and gateway protocol also have no idle-timeout field today, and the strict config/protocol schemas would reject one. This PR keeps the contract additive and opt-in: leaving `talk.idleTimeoutS` unset preserves the existing manual-stop behavior, while setting a positive integer arms idle auto-deactivation.

## Behavior
- `talk.idleTimeoutS` accepts positive integer seconds in config and protocol payloads
- unset, zero, non-integer, and string values stay rejected or normalized away according to the existing config path
- macOS Talk resets idle activity on user speech/transcript updates and when a turn finishes/resumes listening
- the idle timer only fires while Talk is in `listening` with no pending transcript, so it does not replace `silenceTimeoutMs` or cut off thinking/speaking phases
- when the timer expires, Talk disables through `AppStateStore.shared.setTalkEnabled(false)`, which lets the existing controller teardown resume Voice Wake waiting

## Validation
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/zod-schema.talk.test.ts src/config/config.talk-validation.test.ts src/config/talk.normalize.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/talk-config.contract.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/gateway/server.talk-config.test.ts`
